translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 75

sentences.zh: 【魏紀七】起柔兆攝提格，盡玄黓涒灘，凡七年。

translations.literal: [Wei Records Seven] Beginning with Rouzhao-Shetige, ending with Xuanyi-Tuoshan, seven years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Wei Records, Seven] spans from the year Rouzhao-Shetige through Xuanyi-Tuoshan—a period of seven years.

sentences.zh: 邵陵厲公中正始七年（

translations.literal: Deposed Emperor of Shaoling, Zhengshi year seven (
translations.idiomatic: Deposed Emperor of Shaoling, Zhengshi year 7 (

sentences.zh: 丙寅，公元二四六年）

translations.literal: Bingyin, the year 246 of the Common Era)
translations.idiomatic: bingyin cycle, AD 246)

sentences.zh: 春，二月，吳車騎將軍朱然寇柤中，殺略數千人而去。

translations.literal: Spring, second month: Wu's Cavalry General Zhu Ran raided Zhazhong, killed and plundered several thousand people, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of spring, Zhu Ran of Wu, Cavalry General, raided Zhazhong, killing and plundering several thousand people before withdrawing.

sentences.zh: 幽州刺史毌丘儉以高句驪王位宮數為侵叛，督諸軍討之；

translations.literal: Youzhou Inspector Guanqiu Jian, because the King of Gaogouli, Gong, had repeatedly invaded and rebelled, supervised the armies to attack him;
translations.idiomatic: Guanqiu Jian, Inspector of Youzhou, noting that Gong, king of Goguryeo, had repeatedly invaded and rebelled, led the armies in a campaign against him;

sentences.zh: 位宮敗走，儉遂屠丸都，斬獲首虜以千數。

translations.literal: Gong was defeated and fled; Jian then sacked Wandu, beheading and capturing enemies by the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Gong was defeated and fled. Jian sacked Wandu and beheaded or captured more than a thousand of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 句驪之臣得來數諫位宮，位宮不從，得來歎曰：「立見此地將生蓬蒿。

translations.literal: A Goguryeo minister named Deilai had often remonstrated with Gong, but Gong would not heed him. Deilai sighed and said, "Before long this land will grow weeds."
translations.idiomatic: The Goguryeo minister Deilai had often remonstrated with Gong, but Gong would not listen. Deilai sighed and said, "Soon this place will be overgrown with weeds."

sentences.zh: 」遂不食而死。

translations.literal: " Then he starved himself to death.
translations.idiomatic: " He then refused food and died.

sentences.zh: 儉令諸軍不壞其墓，不伐其樹，得其妻子皆放遣之。

translations.literal: Jian ordered the armies not to harm his tomb or cut down his trees, and released his wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: Jian ordered his troops not to damage Deilai's tomb or cut his trees, and sent his wife and children away unharmed.

sentences.zh: 位宮單將妻子逃竄，儉引軍還。

translations.literal: Gong fled alone with his wife and children; Jian led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: Gong fled with only his wife and children. Jian led the army home.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復擊之，位宮遂奔買溝。

translations.literal: Before long he attacked again, and Gong fled to Maigou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Jian attacked again, and Gong fled to Maigou.

sentences.zh: 儉遣玄菟太守王頎追之，過沃沮千有餘里，至肅慎氏南界，刻石紀功而還，所誅、納八千餘口。

translations.literal: Jian sent Xuantu Administrator Wang Qi in pursuit, passing more than a thousand li through Woju, reaching the southern border of the Sushen tribe, carving stone to record the achievement before returning; those executed and taken numbered more than eight thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Jian sent Wang Qi, Administrator of Xuantu, in pursuit. The chase ran more than a thousand li past Woju to the southern border of the Sushen people, where they carved a stone record of the campaign before turning back; those killed or taken captive numbered more than eight thousand.

sentences.zh: 論功受賞，侯者百餘人。

translations.literal: For merit, rewards were distributed; more than a hundred men received marquisates.
translations.idiomatic: Merit was rewarded, and more than a hundred men were enfeoffed as marquises.

sentences.zh: 秋，九月，吳主以驃騎將軍步騭為丞相，車騎將軍朱然為左大司馬，衛將軍全琮為右大司馬。

translations.literal: Autumn, ninth month: Wu's ruler made Flying Cavalry General Bu Zhi Grand Chancellor, Cavalry General Zhu Ran Left Grand Marshal, and Guards General Quan Cong Right Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of autumn, the Wu ruler made Bu Zhi, Flying Cavalry General, Grand Chancellor; Zhu Ran, Cavalry General, Left Grand Marshal; and Quan Cong, Guards General, Right Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 分荊州為二部：以鎮南將軍呂岱為上大將軍，督右部，自武昌以西至蒲圻；

translations.literal: Jing province was divided into two commands: Grand General of the Southern Pacification Lü Dai was made Superior Grand General supervising the right command, from west of Wuchang to Puqi;
translations.idiomatic: Jing was split into two sections: Lü Dai, General of the Southern Pacification, was made Superior Grand General to supervise the western section from Wuchang west to Puqi;

sentences.zh: 以威北將軍諸葛恪為大將軍，督左部，代陸遜鎮武昌。

translations.literal: Mighty North General Zhuge Ke was made Grand General supervising the left command, replacing Lu Xun at Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Ke, Mighty North General, was made Grand General to supervise the eastern section, replacing Lu Xun at Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 漢大赦，大司農河南孟光於眾中責費禕曰：「夫赦者，偏枯之物，非明世所宜有也。

translations.literal: Han declared a great amnesty. Minister of Grand Granary Meng Guang of Henan rebuked Fei Yi in public, saying, "Amnesties are a remedy for partial paralysis, not something a clear age should have."
translations.idiomatic: Han proclaimed a general amnesty. Meng Guang of Henan, Minister of Grand Granary, publicly rebuked Fei Yi: "Amnesty is medicine for a withered limb—not something a bright age ought to rely on."

sentences.zh: 衰敝窮極，必不得已，然後乃可權而行之耳。

translations.literal: When decline and exhaustion reach their limit, one must resort to it from necessity, and only then may one use it as a temporary measure.
translations.idiomatic: When a state is broken and exhausted, there is no choice but to use it, and then only as a last resort.

sentences.zh: 今主上仁賢，百僚稱職，何有旦夕之急，而數施非常之恩，以惠奸宄之惡乎！

translations.literal: Now the sovereign is benevolent and wise, and all officials discharge their duties—what sudden urgency is there that you should repeatedly grant extraordinary favors to benefit wicked criminals!
translations.idiomatic: Now our ruler is humane and his ministers competent. What pressing crisis demands repeated extraordinary pardons that only indulge the wicked?

sentences.zh: 」禕但顧謝，踧□而已。

translations.literal: " Yi could only offer apologies and shrink back abashedly.
translations.idiomatic: " Fei Yi could only apologize and withdraw in embarrassment.

sentences.zh: 初，丞相亮時，有言公惜赦者，亮答曰：「治世以大德，不以小惠，故匡衡、吳漢不願為赦。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Chancellor was in power, someone said the Duke was stingy with amnesties. Liang replied, "In governing an age of order one relies on great virtue, not small favors; therefore Kuang Heng and Wu Han did not wish to grant amnesties."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Zhuge Liang was Chancellor, someone said he was reluctant to grant amnesties. Liang answered, "A well-ordered age is ruled by great virtue, not petty favors—hence Kuang Heng and Wu Han refused to issue pardons."

sentences.zh: 先帝亦言：『吾周旋陳元方、鄭康成間，每見啟告治亂之道悉矣，曾不語赦也。

translations.literal: The late emperor also said, "In my dealings with Chen Yuanfang and Zheng Kangcheng, whenever I heard them expound the ways of order and disorder, they were thorough—yet they never spoke of amnesty."
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor also said, "Among Chen Yuanfang and Zheng Kangcheng I heard every lesson on order and chaos, yet never once did they mention amnesty."

sentences.zh: 若劉景升、季玉父子，歲歲赦宥，何益於治！

translations.literal: If Liu Jingsheng and the father-and-son Jiyu amnestied year after year, what good did it do for governance!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao and Liu Zhang, father and son, pardoned every year—what did that do for good government!

sentences.zh: 』」由是蜀人稱亮之賢，知禕不及焉。

translations.literal: "" From this the people of Shu praised Liang's wisdom and knew Yi did not measure up.
translations.idiomatic: "" From this the people of Shu praised Liang's wisdom and knew Fei Yi fell short of it.

sentences.zh: 陳壽評曰：諸葛亮為政，軍旅數興而赦不妄下，不亦卓乎？

translations.literal: Chen Shou commented: In Zhuge Liang's governance, though campaigns were frequent, amnesties were not issued rashly—is this not outstanding?
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shou remarked: Zhuge Liang governed amid constant warfare yet never issued amnesties lightly—is that not remarkable?

sentences.zh: 吳人不便大錢，乃罷之。

translations.literal: The people of Wu found large coins inconvenient, so they were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Wu found large-denomination coins inconvenient, so the currency was withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 漢主以涼州刺史姜維為衛將軍，與大將軍費禕並錄尚書事。

translations.literal: The Han ruler made Liangzhou Inspector Jiang Wei Guards General, and he together with Grand General Fei Yi jointly recorded matters for the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: The Han ruler made Jiang Wei, Inspector of Liangzhou, Guards General, and he and Grand General Fei Yi jointly oversaw the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 汶山平康夷反，維討平之。

translations.literal: The Pingkang Yi of Wenshan rebelled; Wei campaigned and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: The Pingkang Yi of Wenshan rebelled; Jiang Wei suppressed them.

sentences.zh: 漢主數出遊觀，增廣聲樂。

translations.literal: The Han ruler often went out on excursions and expanded music and entertainment.
translations.idiomatic: The Han ruler went out on pleasure excursions again and again and expanded the palace musicians.

sentences.zh: 太子家令巴西譙周上疏諫曰：「昔王莽之敗，豪傑並起以爭神器，才智之士思望所歸，未必以其勢之廣狹，惟其德之薄厚也。

translations.literal: Household Steward of the Heir Apparent Qiao Zhou of Baxi submitted a memorial remonstrating, saying, "In the past when Wang Mang fell, heroes rose together to contend for the sacred vessel; men of talent and wisdom looked to where their hopes lay—not necessarily according to the breadth or narrowness of their power, but according to the thickness or thinness of their virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Zhou of Baxi, Household Steward of the Heir Apparent, submitted a memorial of remonstrance: "When Wang Mang fell, heroes rose everywhere to seize the Mandate. Men of talent chose whom to follow not by the size of a faction's territory but by the weight of its virtue."

sentences.zh: 於時更始、公孫述等多已廣大，然莫不快情恣欲，怠於為善。

translations.literal: At that time Gengshi, Gongsun Shu, and others had already grown large, yet none failed to indulge their desires and slacken in doing good.
translations.idiomatic: Gengshi, Gongsun Shu, and others already held broad territories, yet each gave free rein to pleasure and neglected virtue.

sentences.zh: 世祖初入河北，馮異等勸之曰：『當行人所不能為者。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor first entered Hebei, Feng Yi and others urged him, saying, "You must do what others cannot do."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangwu first entered Hebei, Feng Yi and others urged him, "Do what others will not do."

sentences.zh: 』遂務理冤獄，崇節儉，北州歌歎，聲布四遠。

translations.literal: " He then devoted himself to redressing wrongful cases, honored frugality, and the northern provinces sang his praise; his renown spread to the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: " He then redressed wrongful convictions, upheld frugality, and songs of praise spread from the northern provinces to the four corners of the realm.

sentences.zh: 於是鄧禹自南陽追之，吳漢、寇恂素未之識，舉兵助之，其餘望風慕德，邳肜、耿純、劉植之徒，至於輿病繼棺，襁負而至，不可勝數，故能以弱為強而成帝業。

translations.literal: Thereupon Deng Yu pursued him from Nanyang; Wu Han and Kou Xun, though they had never known him before, raised troops to aid him. The rest, seeing his virtue from afar, admired it—Pi Yin, Geng Chun, Liu Zhi, and the like, even to the point of carrying the sick on litters and bearing infants on their backs to come; they could not be counted. Thus he was able to turn weakness into strength and accomplish the imperial enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Then Deng Yu followed him from Nanyang; Wu Han and Kou Xun, though strangers, raised armies to help. Others came at the report of his virtue—Pi Yin, Geng Chun, Liu Zhi, and more, even the sick borne on litters and infants on backs, beyond counting—so that he turned weakness into strength and won the empire.

sentences.zh: 及在洛陽，嘗欲小出，銚期進諫，即時還車。

translations.literal: When he was in Luoyang, he once wished to go out briefly; Yao Qi remonstrated, and he immediately turned the carriage back.
translations.idiomatic: Once in Luoyang he wished to slip out briefly; Yao Qi remonstrated, and he turned the carriage back at once.

sentences.zh: 及穎川盜起，寇恂請世祖身往臨賊，聞言即行。

translations.literal: When bandits rose in Yingchuan, Kou Xun asked the Founding Emperor to go in person to face the rebels; on hearing this he set out at once.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose in Yingchuan, Kou Xun asked Guangwu to go in person against them; the emperor set out the moment he heard.

sentences.zh: 故非急務，欲小出不敢；

translations.literal: Thus for non-urgent matters he wished to go out briefly but dared not;
translations.idiomatic: For matters that were not urgent he wished to go out but dared not;

sentences.zh: 至於急務，欲自安不為；

translations.literal: for urgent matters he wished to rest at ease but would not;
translations.idiomatic: for urgent matters he wished to rest but would not;

sentences.zh: 帝者之欲善也如此！

translations.literal: such was an emperor's desire to do good!
translations.idiomatic: such was an emperor's hunger to do good!

sentences.zh: 故《傳》曰：『百姓不徒附』，誠以德先之也。

translations.literal: Therefore the Classic of Documents says, "The common people do not attach themselves for nothing"—truly virtue leads them first.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Documents says, "The people do not attach themselves without reason"—they follow virtue first.

sentences.zh: 今漢遭厄運，天下三分，雄哲之士思望之時也。

translations.literal: Now Han has met with misfortune; the realm is divided in three—this is the time when heroic and wise men turn their hopes.
translations.idiomatic: Han now faces hard fortune and the realm is divided three ways—the hour when heroes and sages fix their hopes.

sentences.zh: 臣願陛下復行人所不能為者，以副人望。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes Your Majesty again to do what others cannot do, to answer the people's hopes.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty again to do what others will not do, and meet the people's hopes.

sentences.zh: 且承事宗廟，所以率民尊上也，今四時之祀或有不臨，而池苑之觀或有仍出，臣之愚滯，私不自安。

translations.literal: Moreover, attending to the ancestral temples is how one leads the people to honor their superiors; now the seasonal sacrifices are sometimes missed, yet excursions to ponds and gardens still occur—your servant's dull stupidity cannot find private peace.
translations.idiomatic: Serving the ancestral temples is how a ruler leads the people to revere what is above; yet now seasonal sacrifices are sometimes missed while visits to parks and ponds continue. In my dullness I cannot be easy in my mind.

sentences.zh: 夫憂責在身者，不暇盡樂，先帝之志，堂構未成，誠非盡樂之時。

translations.literal: One who bears worry and responsibility on his person has no leisure for full enjoyment; the late emperor's intent—the hall and framework not yet completed—truly this is not the time for full enjoyment.
translations.idiomatic: One who bears the weight of rule has no leisure for full pleasure; the late emperor's design—the great work unfinished—is truly not a time for full pleasure.

sentences.zh: 願省減樂官、後宮，凡所增造，但奉修先帝所施，下為子孫節儉之教。

translations.literal: I wish to reduce musicians and the inner palace; all additions should only maintain what the late emperor established, and below set an example of frugality for posterity.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that you reduce musicians and the inner palace, add nothing beyond what the late emperor left, and teach frugality to generations below.

sentences.zh: 」漢主不聽。

translations.literal: " The Han ruler did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: " The Han ruler would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 邵陵厲公中正始八年（

translations.literal: Deposed Emperor of Shaoling, Zhengshi year eight (
translations.idiomatic: Deposed Emperor of Shaoling, Zhengshi year 8 (

sentences.zh: 丁卯，公元二四七年）

translations.literal: Dingmao, the year 247 of the Common Era)
translations.idiomatic: dingmao cycle, AD 247)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，吳全琮卒。

translations.literal: Spring, first month: Quan Cong of Wu died.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, Quan Cong of Wu died.

sentences.zh: 二月，日有食之。

translations.literal: Second month: there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 時尚書何晏等朋附曹爽，好變改法度。

translations.literal: At this time Masters of Writing He Yan and others clung to Cao Shuang and delighted in changing laws and institutions.
translations.idiomatic: At this time He Yan and other Masters of Writing attached themselves to Cao Shuang and were eager to alter laws and institutions.

sentences.zh: 太尉蔣濟上疏曰：「昔大舜佐治，戒在比周；

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Jiang Ji submitted a memorial, saying, "In antiquity when Great Shun assisted in governance, his warning was against factional cliques;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Jiang Ji submitted a memorial: "When Great Shun assisted in rule, he warned against cliques;

sentences.zh: 周公輔政，慎於其朋。

translations.literal: when the Duke of Zhou assisted in government, he was cautious about his associates."
translations.idiomatic: when the Duke of Zhou governed, he was wary of his companions."

sentences.zh: 夫為國法度，惟命世大才，乃能張其綱維以垂於後，豈中下之吏所宜改易哉！

translations.literal: As for a state's laws and institutions, only a great talent of the age can stretch their main cords to hand down to posterity—how could middle and lower officials properly alter them!
translations.idiomatic: A state's laws and institutions can be set aright for posterity only by a heaven-sent genius—how should middle and lower officials be allowed to alter them!

sentences.zh: 終無益於治，適足傷民。

translations.literal: In the end they benefit governance not at all and only harm the people.
translations.idiomatic: They do governance no good and only harm the people.

sentences.zh: 宜使文武之臣，各守其職，率以清平，則和氣祥瑞可感而致也！

translations.literal: Civil and military officials should each keep their duties and lead with clarity and peace—then harmonious qi and auspicious omens may be sensed and obtained!
translations.idiomatic: Let civil and military officials each keep their posts and lead with clarity and peace—then harmonious qi and auspicious omens may be drawn down!

sentences.zh: 吳主詔徙武昌宮材瓦繕修建業宮。

translations.literal: The Wu ruler ordered that timber and tiles from Wuchang Palace be moved to repair and build Jianye Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu ruler ordered timber and tiles from Wuchang Palace moved to repair and expand Jianye Palace.

sentences.zh: 有司奏言：「武昌宮已二十八歲，恐不堪用，宜下所在，通更伐致。

translations.literal: The responsible offices reported, "Wuchang Palace is already twenty-eight years old and may not be fit for use; orders should go down to the districts to fell and deliver timber everywhere."
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices reported, "Wuchang Palace is twenty-eight years old and may no longer be sound; Your Majesty should order timber felled throughout the realm."

sentences.zh: 」吳主曰：「大禹以卑宮為美。

translations.literal: " The Wu ruler said, "Yu the Great took humble palaces as beautiful."
translations.idiomatic: " The Wu ruler said, "Yu the Great prized humble dwellings."

sentences.zh: 今軍事未已，所在賦斂，若更通伐，妨損農桑，徙武昌材瓦，自可用也。

translations.literal: Now warfare is not yet ended and levies are imposed everywhere; if we further order universal felling, it will harm agriculture and sericulture. Moving Wuchang's timber and tiles can be used as they are.
translations.idiomatic: War has not ended and levies press on every district; more universal timber-cutting would harm farming. Wuchang's timber and tiles will serve well enough.

sentences.zh: 」乃徙居南宮。

translations.literal: " He then moved residence to the Southern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: " He then took up residence in the Southern Palace.

sentences.zh: 三月，改作太初宮，令諸將及州郡皆義作。

translations.literal: Third month: the Taichu Palace was rebuilt, and generals and provinces were all ordered to contribute labor as a duty.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the Taichu Palace was rebuilt, and generals and provinces were ordered to supply labor as a public duty.

sentences.zh: 大將軍爽用何晏、鄧颺、丁謐之謀，遷太后於永寧宮；

translations.literal: Grand General Shuang, using the plans of He Yan, Deng Yang, and Ding Mi, moved the Empress Dowager to Yongning Palace;
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Cao Shuang, following the counsel of He Yan, Deng Yang, and Ding Mi, moved the Empress Dowager to Yongning Palace;

sentences.zh: 專擅朝政，多樹親黨，屢改制度。

translations.literal: monopolized court governance, planted many personal factions, and repeatedly altered institutions.
translations.idiomatic: monopolized the government, built up a private faction, and altered institutions again and again.

sentences.zh: 太傅懿不能禁，與爽有隙。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Yi could not restrain him and had a rift with Shuang.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Sima Yi could not restrain him and grew estranged from Shuang.

sentences.zh: 五月，懿始稱疾，不與政事。

translations.literal: Fifth month: Yi first claimed illness and did not attend to government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Yi first claimed illness and withdrew from government.

sentences.zh: 吳丞相步騭卒。

translations.literal: Grand Chancellor Bu Zhi of Wu died.
translations.idiomatic: Bu Zhi, Grand Chancellor of Wu, died.

sentences.zh: 帝好褻近群小，游宴後園。

translations.literal: The emperor delighted in familiar intimacy with petty men and feasted and played in the rear garden.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor delighted in the company of petty favorites and feasted in the rear garden.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，尚書何晏上言：「自今御幸式乾殿及遊豫後園，宜皆從大臣，詢謀政事，講論經義，為萬世法。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: Master of Writing He Yan submitted a statement, saying, "From now on when Your Majesty visits the Shigan Hall or roams and plays in the rear garden, you should always be accompanied by great ministers, consulting on government affairs and discussing the classics and their meaning, to set an example for ten thousand generations."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, He Yan submitted a memorial: "When Your Majesty visits the Shigan Hall or the rear garden hereafter, great ministers should accompany you to discuss government and the classics, setting an example for ages to come."

sentences.zh: 」冬，十二月，散騎常侍、諫議大夫孔乂上言：「今天下已平，陛下可絕後園習騎乘馬，出必御輦乘車，天下之福，臣子之願也。

translations.literal: Winter, twelfth month: Regular Attendant and Grand Remonstrator Kong Yi submitted a statement, saying, "Now the realm is already at peace; Your Majesty may cease practicing horsemanship in the rear garden and, when going out, always ride the imperial carriage—this would be the realm's blessing and your servants' wish."
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of winter, Kong Yi submitted a memorial: "The realm is at peace; Your Majesty should cease riding in the rear garden and always use the imperial carriage when you go out—the blessing of the empire and the wish of your servants."

sentences.zh: 」帝皆不聽。

translations.literal: " The emperor did not listen to any of it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor would not heed either.

sentences.zh: 吳主大發眾集建業，揚聲欲入寇。

translations.literal: The Wu ruler greatly mobilized troops and gathered them at Jianye, proclaiming loudly that he intended to invade.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu ruler mobilized a great host at Jianye and proclaimed an intention to invade.

sentences.zh: 揚州刺史諸葛誕使安豐太守王基策之，基曰：「今陸遜等已死，孫權年老，內無賢嗣，中無謀主。

translations.literal: Yangzhou Inspector Zhuge Dan had Anfeng Administrator Wang Ji assess the situation. Ji said, "Now Lu Xun and the like are dead; Sun Quan is old; within there is no worthy heir, and in the center there is no strategist."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Dan, Inspector of Yangzhou, had Wang Ji, Administrator of Anfeng, assess the situation. Ji said, "Lu Xun and the rest are dead; Sun Quan is old; within he has no worthy heir, and at court no strategist."

sentences.zh: 權自出則懼內釁卒起，癰疽發潰；

translations.literal: If Quan goes out himself he fears internal strife will suddenly arise and an abscess will burst;
translations.idiomatic: If Quan goes in person he fears sudden rebellion within, like an abscess bursting;

sentences.zh: 遣將則舊將已盡，新將未信。

translations.literal: if he sends a general, the old generals are already gone and the new ones are not yet trusted.
translations.idiomatic: if he sends a general, the old commanders are gone and the new ones are not trusted.

sentences.zh: 此不過欲補衣定支黨，還自保護耳。

translations.literal: This is nothing more than wishing to patch garments and settle factions, then return to protect himself.
translations.idiomatic: This is only patching his house and settling his faction—then returning to protect himself.

sentences.zh: 」已而吳果不出。

translations.literal: " Before long Wu indeed did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end Wu did not march out.

sentences.zh: 是歲，雍、涼羌胡叛降漢，漢姜維將兵出隴右以應之，與雍州刺史郭淮、討蜀護軍夏侯霸戰於洮西。

translations.literal: This year the Qiang and Hu of Yong and Liang rebelled and submitted to Han. Han's Jiang Wei led troops out through Longyou to respond, and fought with Yongzhou Inspector Guo Huai and Protector of the Army Against Shu Xiahou Ba at the west of the Tao River.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Qiang and Hu of Yong and Liang rebelled and submitted to Han. Jiang Wei led troops through Longyou to meet them and fought Guo Huai, Inspector of Yongzhou, and Xiahou Ba, Protector of the Army Against Shu, west of the Tao.

sentences.zh: 胡王白虎文、治無戴等率部落降維，維徙之入蜀。

translations.literal: Hu kings Baihuwen, Zhiwudai, and others led their tribes to submit to Wei; Wei moved them into Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Hu kings Baihuwen, Zhiwudai, and others led their tribes to submit to Jiang Wei, who resettled them in Shu.

sentences.zh: 淮進擊羌胡餘黨，皆平之。

translations.literal: Huai advanced to attack the remaining Qiang and Hu parties and pacified them all.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Huai advanced against the remaining Qiang and Hu bands and pacified them all.

sentences.zh: 邵陵厲公中正始九年（

translations.literal: Deposed Emperor of Shaoling, Zhengshi year nine (
translations.idiomatic: Deposed Emperor of Shaoling, Zhengshi year 9 (

sentences.zh: 戊辰，公元二四八年）

translations.literal: Wuchen, the year 248 of the Common Era)
translations.idiomatic: wuchen cycle, AD 248)

sentences.zh: 春，二月，中書令孫資，癸巳，中書監劉放，三月，甲午，司徒衛臻各遜位，以侯就第，位特進。

translations.literal: Spring, second month: Director of the Secretariat Sun Zi; on guisi day, Supervisor of the Secretariat Liu Fang; third month, on jiawu day, Minister over the Masses Wei Zhen each yielded office, took marquis rank and retired to their estates, and held the eminent position of Special Advancement.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of spring, Sun Zi, Director of the Secretariat, on the guisi day; Liu Fang, Supervisor of the Secretariat, in the third month on the jiawu day; and Wei Zhen, Minister over the Masses—each retired, took up residence as a marquis, and held the rank of Special Advancement.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，以司空高柔為司徒，光祿大夫徐邈為司空。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month: Minister of Works Gao Rou was made Minister over the Masses, and Household Minister Xu Miao was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, Gao Rou, Minister of Works, was made Minister over the Masses, and Xu Miao, Household Minister, was made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 邈歎曰：「三公論道之官，無其人則缺，豈可以老病忝之哉！

translations.literal: Miao sighed and said, "The Three Excellencies are offices for expounding the Way; if there is no fit man the post should remain vacant—how can one disgrace it with old age and illness!"
translations.idiomatic: Xu Miao sighed and said, "The Three Excellencies are posts for expounding the Way; if no worthy man exists the office should stand empty—how can I disgrace it with age and illness!"

sentences.zh: 」遂固辭不受。

translations.literal: " He firmly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: " He firmly declined and would not accept.

sentences.zh: 五月，漢費禕出屯漢中。

translations.literal: Fifth month: Fei Yi of Han went out to garrison Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Fei Yi of Han went out to garrison Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 自蔣琬及禕，雖身居於外，慶賞威刑，皆遙先咨斷，然後乃行。

translations.literal: From Jiang Wan through Yi, though their persons were stationed outside, rewards, punishments, and authority were all first consulted and decided from afar before being carried out.
translations.idiomatic: From Jiang Wan through Fei Yi, though they served far from the capital, rewards and punishments were always decided by consultation from afar before being executed.

sentences.zh: 禕雅性謙素，當國功名，略與琬比。

translations.literal: Yi by nature was modest and plain; in governing the state his achievements were roughly comparable to Wan's.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Yi was modest by nature, and his achievements in governing the state were roughly on a par with Jiang Wan's.

sentences.zh: 秋，九月，以車騎將軍王凌為司空。

translations.literal: Autumn, ninth month: Cavalry General Wang Ling was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of autumn, Wang Ling, Cavalry General, was made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 陪陵夷反，漢車騎將軍鄧芝討平之。

translations.literal: The Peiling Yi rebelled; Han's Cavalry General Deng Zhi campaigned and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: The Peiling Yi rebelled; Deng Zhi, Cavalry General of Han, suppressed them.

sentences.zh: 大將軍爽，驕奢無度，飲食衣服，擬於乘輿；

translations.literal: Grand General Shuang was arrogant and extravagant beyond measure; food, drink, and clothing rivaled the imperial carriage;
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Cao Shuang was arrogant and extravagant beyond measure; his food, drink, and dress rivaled the emperor's;

sentences.zh: 尚方珍玩，充牣其家；

translations.literal: precious curios from the imperial workshops filled his house;
translations.idiomatic: precious curios from the imperial workshops filled his house;

sentences.zh: 又私取先帝才人以為伎樂。

translations.literal: he also privately took the late emperor's talented women for musicians and entertainers.
translations.idiomatic: he also privately took the late emperor's talented women for musicians and entertainers.

sentences.zh: 作窟室，綺疏四周，數與其黨何晏等縱酒其中。

translations.literal: He built a cave chamber with carved lattices on all sides and often drank freely there with his faction He Yan and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: He built a vaulted chamber with carved lattices on every side and often drank there with his clique, He Yan and the rest.

sentences.zh: 弟羲深以為憂，數涕泣諫止之，爽不聽。

translations.literal: His younger brother Xi was deeply worried and repeatedly wept and remonstrated to stop him; Shuang would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Cao Xi was deeply troubled and repeatedly wept and remonstrated with him; Shuang would not listen.

sentences.zh: 爽兄弟數俱出遊，司農沛國桓范謂曰：「總萬機，典禁兵，不宜並出。

translations.literal: The Shuang brothers often went out touring together. Minister of Agriculture Huan Fan of Peiguo said to them, "You hold all affairs of state and command the forbidden troops—it is not fitting to go out together."
translations.idiomatic: The Shuang brothers often went out touring together. Huan Fan of Peiguo, Minister of Agriculture, said to them, "You hold all affairs of state and command the forbidden troops—you should not go out together."

sentences.zh: 若有閉城門，誰復內入者？

translations.literal: If someone should shut the city gates, who could get back in?
translations.idiomatic: If someone shuts the city gates, who will be let back in?

sentences.zh: 」爽曰：「誰敢爾邪！

translations.literal: " Shuang said, "Who would dare do such a thing!"
translations.idiomatic: " Shuang said, "Who would dare!"

sentences.zh: 初，清河、平原爭界，八年不能決。

translations.literal: Earlier, Qinghe and Pingyuan disputed their border; for eight years it could not be decided.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Qinghe and Pingyuan disputed their border, and for eight years the matter could not be settled.

sentences.zh: 冀州刺史孫禮請天府所藏烈祖封平原時圖以決之。

translations.literal: Jizhou Inspector Sun Li requested the map stored in the imperial treasury from when the Illustrious Ancestor enfeoffed Pingyuan to decide it.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Li, Inspector of Jizhou, asked to use the map in the imperial treasury from when Emperor Ming enfeoffed Pingyuan to settle the dispute.

sentences.zh: 爽信清河之訴，雲圖不可用，禮上疏自辨，辭頗剛切。

translations.literal: Shuang trusted Qinghe's petition, saying the map could not be used. Li submitted a memorial in self-defense, his words rather stern.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang sided with Qinghe and said the map could not be used. Sun Li submitted a self-defense memorial in rather sharp language.

sentences.zh: 爽大怒，劾禮怨望，結刑五歲。

translations.literal: Shuang was greatly angered, impeached Li for resentment, and fixed his punishment at five years.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang was furious, impeached Sun Li for resentment, and sentenced him to five years.

sentences.zh: 久之，復為并州刺史，往見太傅懿，有忿色而無言。

translations.literal: After a long while he was again made Bingzhou Inspector and went to see Grand Tutor Yi with an angry look but said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he was again made Inspector of Bingzhou and went to see Grand Tutor Sima Yi with an angry face but said nothing.

sentences.zh: 懿曰：「卿得并州少邪？

translations.literal: Yi said, "Do you find Bingzhou too small?
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "Do you find Bingzhou too small?

sentences.zh: 恚理分界失分乎？

translations.literal: Are you resentful that the boundary dispute went against you?"
translations.idiomatic: Are you angry that the boundary ruling went against you?"

sentences.zh: 」禮曰：「何明公言之乖也！

translations.literal: " Li said, "How far from the mark, my lord, is what you say!
translations.idiomatic: " Sun Li said, "How mistaken you are, my lord!

sentences.zh: 禮雖不德，豈以官位往事為意邪！

translations.literal: Though Li lacks virtue, how could he take office and past affairs to heart!
translations.idiomatic: Though I lack virtue, would I brood over offices and past affairs!

sentences.zh: 本謂明公齊蹤伊、呂，匡輔魏室，上報明帝之托，下建萬世之勳。

translations.literal: I had thought my lord would equal Yi Yin and Lü Shang, support and assist the house of Wei, answer above Emperor Ming's entrustment, and below establish merit for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: I had thought you would follow Yi Yin and Lü Shang, support the house of Wei, fulfill Emperor Ming's trust above, and build lasting merit below.

sentences.zh: 今社稷將危，天下凶凶，此禮之所以不悅也！

translations.literal: Now the altars of state are about to be endangered and the realm is in turmoil—this is why Li is displeased!
translations.idiomatic: Now the altars of state are in peril and the realm is in turmoil—that is why I am displeased!

sentences.zh: 」因涕泣橫流。

translations.literal: " Thereupon tears streamed across his face.
translations.idiomatic: " Tears streamed down his face.

sentences.zh: 懿曰：「且止，忍不可忍！

translations.literal: Yi said, "Stop for now—what cannot be endured must be endured!
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "Enough for now—endure what cannot be endured!

sentences.zh: 冬，河南尹李勝出為荊州刺史，過辭太傅懿。

translations.literal: Winter: Intendant of Henan Li Sheng went out as Jingzhou Inspector and stopped to take leave of Grand Tutor Yi.
translations.idiomatic: In winter Li Sheng, Intendant of Henan, went out as Inspector of Jingzhou and stopped to bid farewell to Grand Tutor Sima Yi.

sentences.zh: 懿令兩婢侍，持衣，衣落；

translations.literal: Yi had two maidservants attend him; they held his clothes and the clothes fell;
translations.idiomatic: Yi had two maidservants attend him; they held his clothes and the clothes fell;

sentences.zh: 指口言渴，婢進粥，懿不持杯而飲，粥皆流出沾胸。

translations.literal: he pointed to his mouth saying he was thirsty; a maid brought porridge; Yi did not hold the cup but drank, and the porridge all ran out and stained his chest.
translations.idiomatic: he pointed to his mouth and said he was thirsty; a maid brought porridge; Yi drank without holding the cup, and the porridge ran down and stained his chest.

sentences.zh: 勝曰：「眾情謂明公舊風發動，何意尊體乃爾！

translations.literal: Sheng said, "Popular opinion holds that my lord's old ailment has flared up—who would have thought your honored person was like this!"
translations.idiomatic: Sheng said, "Everyone thought your old ailment had returned—who would have thought you were in such a state!"

sentences.zh: 」懿使聲氣才屬，說：「年老枕疾，死在旦夕。

translations.literal: " Yi made his voice just carry and said, "I am old and bedridden with illness; death is at hand.
translations.idiomatic: " Yi made his voice barely carry and said, "I am old and bedridden; death is near.

sentences.zh: 君當屈并州，并州近胡，好為之備！

translations.literal: You should condescend to Bingzhou—Bingzhou is near the Hu; take good care to prepare!
translations.idiomatic: You are bound for Bingzhou—Bingzhou borders the Hu; take good care to prepare!

sentences.zh: 恐不復相見，以子師、昭兄弟為托。

translations.literal: I fear we shall not meet again; I entrust my sons Shi and Zhao and their brothers to you.
translations.idiomatic: I fear we shall not meet again; I entrust my sons Shi and Zhao to you.

sentences.zh: 」勝曰：「當還忝本州，非并州。

translations.literal: " Sheng said, "I am to return to my native province in disgrace—not Bingzhou."
translations.idiomatic: " Sheng said, "I am to return to my native province—not Bingzhou."

sentences.zh: 」懿乃錯亂其辭曰：「君方到并州？

translations.literal: " Yi then confused his words and said, "Are you just now arriving at Bingzhou?"
translations.idiomatic: " Yi then muddled his words and said, "Are you just now arriving at Bingzhou?"

sentences.zh: 」勝復曰：「當忝荊州。

translations.literal: " Sheng again said, "I am to take Jingzhou in disgrace."
translations.idiomatic: " Sheng again said, "I am bound for Jingzhou."

sentences.zh: 」懿曰：「年老意荒，不解君言。

translations.literal: " Yi said, "Old age has muddled my mind; I do not understand your words.
translations.idiomatic: " Yi said, "Old age has muddled my mind; I do not understand you.

sentences.zh: 今還為本州，盛德壯烈，好建功勳！

translations.literal: Now you return to your native province—great virtue and fierce spirit; do good to achieve merit!"
translations.idiomatic: Now you return to your native province—great virtue and fierce spirit; achieve merit!"

sentences.zh: 」勝退，告爽曰：「司馬公屍居餘氣，形神已離，不足慮矣。

translations.literal: " Sheng withdrew and told Shuang, "Lord Sima is a corpse with breath remaining; body and spirit are already parted—he is not worth worrying over."
translations.idiomatic: " Sheng withdrew and told Shuang, "Lord Sima is a corpse with breath remaining; body and spirit are already parted—not worth worrying over."

sentences.zh: 」他日，又向爽等垂泣曰：「太傅病不可復濟，令人愴然！

translations.literal: " Another day he again wept before Shuang and the rest, saying, "The Grand Tutor's illness cannot recover—it is deeply moving!"
translations.idiomatic: " Another day he wept before Shuang and the rest again: "The Grand Tutor's illness cannot recover—it is deeply moving!"

sentences.zh: 」故爽等不復設備。

translations.literal: " Therefore Shuang and the rest no longer made preparations.
translations.idiomatic: " So Shuang and the rest no longer made preparations.

sentences.zh: 何晏聞平原管輅明於術數，請與相見。

translations.literal: He Yan heard that Guan Lu of Pingyuan was skilled in numerology and arts and invited him to meet.
translations.idiomatic: He Yan heard that Guan Lu of Pingyuan was skilled in divination and invited him to meet.

sentences.zh: 十二月，丙戌，輅往詣晏，晏與之論《易》。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, on bingxu day, Lu went to call on Yan, and Yan discussed the Changes with him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the bingxu day, Guan Lu called on He Yan, and He Yan discussed the Changes with him.

sentences.zh: 時鄧颺在坐，謂輅曰：「君自謂善《易》，而語初不及《易》中辭義，何也？

translations.literal: At the time Deng Yang was seated and said to Lu, "You claim to be skilled in the Changes, yet your words at first do not touch the text and meaning within the Changes—why?"
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yang was present and said to Guan Lu, "You claim to be skilled in the Changes, yet you never touch its text and meaning—why?"

sentences.zh: 」輅曰：「夫善《易》者不言《易》也。

translations.literal: " Lu said, "One who is truly skilled in the Changes does not speak of the Changes."
translations.idiomatic: " Guan Lu said, "One who is truly skilled in the Changes does not speak of the Changes."

sentences.zh: 」晏含笑贊之曰：「可謂要言不煩也！

translations.literal: " Yan smiled and praised him, saying, "This may be called essential words without fuss!"
translations.idiomatic: " He Yan smiled and praised him: "Truly essential words without fuss!"

sentences.zh: 」因謂輅曰：「試為作一卦，知位當至三公不？

translations.literal: " He then said to Lu, "Try casting a hexagram for me—will my rank reach the Three Excellencies?"
translations.idiomatic: " He then asked Guan Lu, "Cast a hexagram for me—will I reach the Three Excellencies?"

sentences.zh: 」又問：「連夢見青蠅數十，來集鼻上，驅之不去，何也？

translations.literal: " He also asked, "I have repeatedly dreamed of several tens of green flies coming to gather on my nose; driven away they will not leave—what is this?"
translations.idiomatic: " He also asked, "I have repeatedly dreamed of dozens of green flies gathering on my nose; I drive them away but they will not leave—what does this mean?"

sentences.zh: 」輅曰：「昔元、凱輔舜，周公佐周，皆以和惠謙恭，享有多福，此非卜筮所能明也。

translations.literal: " Lu said, "In antiquity Yuan and Kai assisted Shun, and the Duke of Zhou assisted Zhou—all by harmony, kindness, humility, and respect enjoyed abundant blessing; this is not what divination by stalks and tortoise can make clear."
translations.idiomatic: " Guan Lu said, "In antiquity Yuan and Kai assisted Shun and the Duke of Zhou assisted Zhou—all through harmony, kindness, humility, and respect, and enjoyed abundant blessing. That is not what divination can reveal."

sentences.zh: 今君侯位尊勢重，而懷德者鮮，畏威者眾，殆非小心求福之道也。

translations.literal: Now my lord's rank is exalted and power heavy, yet those cherishing virtue are few and those fearing authority are many—this is scarcely the way of careful seeking for blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Now your rank is exalted and your power heavy, yet few cherish virtue and many fear authority—this is scarcely the way to seek blessing with care.

sentences.zh: 又，鼻者天中之山，『高而不危，所以長守貴。

translations.literal: Moreover, the nose is the mountain at the center of heaven: "High yet not perilous—therefore long to keep nobility."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the nose is the mountain at the center of heaven: "High yet not perilous—therefore long to keep nobility."

sentences.zh: 』今青蠅臭惡而集之，位峻者顛，輕豪者亡，不可不深思也！

translations.literal: " Now green flies, foul and vile, gather on it—those in lofty position topple, the lightly arrogant perish; this cannot but be deeply pondered!
translations.idiomatic: " Now foul green flies gather on it—those in lofty position topple, the lightly arrogant perish; you must ponder this deeply!

sentences.zh: 願君侯裒多益寡，非禮不履，然後三公可至，青蠅可驅也。

translations.literal: I wish my lord would reduce the many and increase the few, tread nothing contrary to ritual—then the Three Excellencies may be reached and the green flies driven away.
translations.idiomatic: I wish you would reduce the many and increase the few, tread nothing contrary to ritual—then the Three Excellencies may be reached and the green flies driven away.

sentences.zh: 」颺曰：「此老生之常譚。

translations.literal: " Yang said, "This is the old pedant's usual chatter."
translations.idiomatic: " Deng Yang said, "This is the old pedant's usual chatter."

sentences.zh: 」輅曰：「夫老生者見不生，常譚者見不譚。

translations.literal: " Lu said, "The old pedant sees no life; the usual chatterer sees no talk."
translations.idiomatic: " Guan Lu said, "The old pedant sees no life; the usual chatterer sees no talk."

sentences.zh: 」輅還邑捨，具以語其舅。

translations.literal: " Lu returned to his lodging in the district and told his uncle everything.
translations.idiomatic: " Guan Lu returned to his lodging and told his uncle everything.

sentences.zh: 舅責輅言太切至，輅曰：「與死人語，何所畏邪！

translations.literal: His uncle reproached Lu for speaking too bluntly. Lu said, "When speaking with dead men, what is there to fear!"
translations.idiomatic: His uncle reproached Guan Lu for speaking too bluntly. Guan Lu said, "When speaking with dead men, what is there to fear!"

sentences.zh: 」舅大怒，以輅為狂。

translations.literal: " His uncle was greatly angered and considered Lu mad.
translations.idiomatic: " His uncle was furious and considered him mad.

sentences.zh: 吳交趾、九真夷賊攻沒城邑，交部騷動。

translations.literal: In Wu, Yi bandits of Jiaozhi and Jiuzhen attacked and overran cities and towns; the Jiao commandery was in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: In Wu, Yi bandits of Jiaozhi and Jiuzhen overran cities and towns, and the Jiao region was in turmoil.

sentences.zh: 吳主以衡陽督軍都尉陸胤為交州刺史、安南校尉。

translations.literal: The Wu ruler made Hengyang Supervisor of Armies Commandant Lu Yin Jiaozhou Inspector and Pacifier of the South Colonel.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu ruler made Lu Yin, Commandant Supervisor of Armies at Hengyang, Inspector of Jiaozhou and Pacifier of the South Colonel.

sentences.zh: 胤入境，喻以恩信，降者五萬餘家，州境復清。

translations.literal: Yin entered the territory and instructed them with kindness and trust; more than fifty thousand households submitted, and the province's borders were again at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yin entered the territory and won them with kindness and trust; more than fifty thousand households submitted, and the province was pacified.

sentences.zh: 太傅懿陰與其子中護軍師、散騎常侍昭謀誅曹爽。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Yi secretly with his sons Central Protector of the Army Shi and Regular Attendant Zhao plotted to execute Cao Shuang.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Sima Yi secretly plotted with his sons Shi, Central Protector of the Army, and Zhao, Regular Attendant, to kill Cao Shuang.

sentences.zh: 邵陵厲公中嘉平元年（

translations.literal: Deposed Emperor of Shaoling, Jiaping year one (
translations.idiomatic: Deposed Emperor of Shaoling, Jiaping year 1 (

sentences.zh: 己巳，公元二四九年）

translations.literal: Jisi, the year 249 of the Common Era)
translations.idiomatic: jisi cycle, AD 249)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，甲午，帝謁高平陵，大將軍爽與弟中領軍羲、武衛將軍訓、散騎常侍彥皆從。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on jiawu day: the emperor visited the Gaoping Tombs. Grand General Shuang with his younger brothers Central Protector of the Army Xi, Martial Guards General Xun, and Regular Attendant Yan all followed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, on the jiawu day, the emperor visited the Gaoping Tombs. Grand General Cao Shuang and his younger brothers Xi, Central Protector of the Army, Xun, Martial Guards General, and Yan, Regular Attendant, all accompanied him.

sentences.zh: 太傅懿以皇太后令，閉諸城門，勒兵據武庫，授兵出屯洛水浮橋，召司徒高柔假節行大將軍事，據爽營，太僕王觀行中領軍事，據羲營。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Yi, by the Empress Dowager's order, closed all city gates, mustered troops and seized the armory, issued arms and went out to garrison the Luo River pontoon bridge, summoned Minister over the Masses Gao Rou with borrowed tally to act as Grand General, and seized Shuang's camp; Minister of Coaches Wang Guan acted as Central Protector of the Army and seized Xi's camp.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Sima Yi, by the Empress Dowager's order, closed all city gates, mustered troops and seized the armory, issued arms and garrisoned the Luo River pontoon bridge, summoned Gao Rou, Minister over the Masses, with borrowed tally to act as Grand General and seize Shuang's camp, and Wang Guan, Minister of Coaches, to act as Central Protector of the Army and seize Xi's camp.

sentences.zh: 因奏爽罪惡於帝曰；

translations.literal: He then memorialized Shuang's crimes to the emperor, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized Shuang's crimes to the emperor:

sentences.zh: 「臣昔從遼東還，先帝詔陛下、秦王及臣升御床，把臣臂，深以後事為念。

translations.literal: " When your servant once returned from Liaodong, the late emperor ordered Your Majesty, the Prince of Qin, and your servant to ascend the imperial couch. He grasped your servant's arm and was deeply concerned about affairs thereafter.
translations.idiomatic: " When I once returned from Liaodong, the late emperor ordered Your Majesty, the Prince of Qin, and me to ascend the imperial couch. He grasped my arm and was deeply concerned about affairs thereafter.

sentences.zh: 臣言『太祖、高祖亦屬臣以後事，此自陛下所見，無所憂苦。

translations.literal: Your servant said, "The Founding Emperor and the High Emperor also entrusted later affairs to your servant—this Your Majesty has yourself seen; there is nothing to worry over.
translations.idiomatic: I said, "The Founding Emperor and the High Emperor also entrusted later affairs to me—this Your Majesty has yourself seen; there is nothing to worry over.

sentences.zh: 萬一有不如意，臣當以死奉明詔。

translations.literal: If by any chance things should not go as wished, your servant will die upholding the enlightened edict."
translations.idiomatic: If by any chance things should not go as wished, I will die upholding the enlightened edict."

sentences.zh: 』今大將軍爽，背棄顧命，敗亂國典，內則僭擬，外則專權，破壞諸營，盡據禁兵，群官要職，皆置所親，殿中宿衛，易以私人，根據盤互，縱恣日甚，又以黃門張當為都監，伺察至尊，離間二宮，傷害骨肉，天下洶洶，人懷危懼。

translations.literal: Now Grand General Shuang has turned his back on the dying charge, ruined the state's institutions, within usurped likeness and without monopolized authority, destroyed the various camps and fully seized the forbidden troops, placed his intimates in all key offices of the bureaucracy, replaced the palace guards with private men, his roots and holdings intertwined, his license growing daily; he also made Yellow Gate Zhang Dang chief overseer to spy on the Supreme One, estrange the two palaces, and harm flesh and bone. The realm is in uproar and men harbor dread.
translations.idiomatic: Now Grand General Shuang has betrayed the dying charge, ruined the state's institutions, usurped authority within and monopolized power without, destroyed the camps and seized the forbidden troops, placed his intimates in all key offices, replaced the palace guards with private men, and grown more licentious daily. He made Zhang Dang of the Yellow Gate chief overseer to spy on Your Majesty, estrange the two palaces, and harm your kin. The realm is in uproar and men live in dread.

sentences.zh: 陛下便為寄坐，豈得久安！

translations.literal: Your Majesty would then be a guest on the throne—how could you long remain secure!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty would then be a guest on the throne—how could you long remain secure!

sentences.zh: 此非先帝詔陛下及臣升御床之本意也。

translations.literal: This was not the late emperor's intent when he ordered Your Majesty and your servant to ascend the imperial couch.
translations.idiomatic: This was not the late emperor's intent when he ordered Your Majesty and me to ascend the imperial couch.

sentences.zh: 臣雖朽邁，敢忘往言！

translations.literal: Though your servant is decayed and aged, how dare he forget his former words!
translations.idiomatic: Though I am decayed and aged, how dare I forget my former words!

sentences.zh: 太尉臣濟等皆以爽為有無君之心，兄弟不宜典兵宿衛，奏永寧宮，皇太后令敕臣如奏施行。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant your servant Ji and others all hold that Shuang has a heart without a ruler; the brothers are not fit to command troops and guard the palace. They memorialized Yongning Palace, and the Empress Dowager ordered your servant to carry out the memorial as submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Jiang Ji and others all hold that Shuang lacks loyalty to his ruler; the brothers are not fit to command troops and guard the palace. They memorialized Yongning Palace, and the Empress Dowager ordered me to carry out the memorial as submitted.

sentences.zh: 臣輒敕主者及黃門令『罷爽、羲、訓吏兵，以侯就第，不得逗留，以稽車駕；

translations.literal: Your servant has immediately ordered the chief clerk and the Director of the Yellow Gate: "Dismiss the officials and troops of Shuang, Xi, and Xun; let them take marquis rank and retire to their estates; they may not linger and delay the imperial carriage;
translations.idiomatic: I have immediately ordered the chief clerk and the Director of the Yellow Gate: "Dismiss the officials and troops of Shuang, Xi, and Xun; let them take marquis rank and retire to their estates; they may not linger and delay the imperial carriage;

sentences.zh: 敢有稽留，便以軍法從事！

translations.literal: whoever dares linger shall be dealt with by military law!"
translations.idiomatic: whoever dares linger shall be dealt with by military law!"

sentences.zh: 』臣輒力疾將兵屯洛水浮橋，伺察非常。

translations.literal: Your servant has immediately, though ill, led troops to garrison the Luo River pontoon bridge and watch for the unusual."
translations.idiomatic: I have immediately, though ill, led troops to garrison the Luo River pontoon bridge and watch for the unusual."

sentences.zh: 」爽得懿奏事，不通；

translations.literal: " Shuang received Yi's memorial but could not get through;
translations.idiomatic: " Shuang received Yi's memorial but could not get through;

sentences.zh: 迫窘不知所為，留車駕宿伊水南，伐木為鹿角，發屯田兵數千人以為衛。

translations.literal: pressed and distressed, he knew not what to do. He kept the imperial carriage to lodge south of the Yi River, felled trees for palisades, and mobilized several thousand garrison-farm soldiers as guards.
translations.idiomatic: pressed and distressed, he knew not what to do. He kept the imperial carriage to lodge south of the Yi River, felled trees for palisades, and mobilized several thousand garrison-farm soldiers as guards.

sentences.zh: 懿使侍中高陽、許允及尚書陳泰說爽宜早自歸罪，又使爽所信殿中校尉尹大目謂爽，唯免官而已，以洛水為誓。

translations.literal: Yi sent Attendant Within Gao Yang, Xu Yun, and Master of Writing Chen Tai to persuade Shuang that he should early submit himself to judgment; he also sent Palace Commandant Yin Damu, whom Shuang trusted, to tell Shuang that he would only be dismissed from office, swearing by the Luo River.
translations.idiomatic: Yi sent Gao Yang and Xu Yun, Attendants Within, and Chen Tai, Master of Writing, to persuade Shuang to submit early; he also sent Yin Damu, Palace Commandant, whom Shuang trusted, to tell him he would only be dismissed from office, swearing by the Luo River.

sentences.zh: 泰，群之子也。

translations.literal: Tai was the son of Qun.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Tai was the son of Chen Qun.

sentences.zh: 初，爽以桓范鄉里老宿，於九卿中特禮之，然不甚親也。

translations.literal: Earlier, Shuang, because Huan Fan was an elder of his native place, treated him with special ceremony among the Nine Ministers, yet was not very close to him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, because Huan Fan was an elder of his native place, Shuang treated him with special ceremony among the Nine Ministers, yet was not very close to him.

sentences.zh: 及懿起兵，以太后令召范，欲使行中領軍。

translations.literal: When Yi raised troops, by the Empress Dowager's order he summoned Fan, intending to have him act as Central Protector of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi raised troops, by the Empress Dowager's order he summoned Fan, intending to have him act as Central Protector of the Army.

sentences.zh: 范欲應命，其子止之曰：「車駕在外，不如南出。

translations.literal: Fan wished to answer the summons; his son stopped him, saying, "The imperial carriage is outside—better to go out south."
translations.idiomatic: Fan wished to answer the summons; his son stopped him: "The imperial carriage is outside—better to go out south."

sentences.zh: 」范乃出。

translations.literal: " Fan then went out.
translations.idiomatic: " Fan then went out.

sentences.zh: 至平昌城門，城門已閉。

translations.literal: When he reached the Pingchang gate, the gate was already closed.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the Pingchang gate, the gate was already closed.

sentences.zh: 門候司蕃，故范舉吏也，范舉手中版以示之，矯曰：「有詔召我，卿促開門！

translations.literal: Gate warden Si Fan, once a clerk Fan had recommended, received him. Fan raised the tablet in his hand to show him and falsely said, "There is an edict summoning me—hurry and open the gate!"
translations.idiomatic: Gate warden Si Fan, once a clerk Fan had recommended, received him. Fan raised the tablet in his hand and falsely said, "There is an edict summoning me—open the gate at once!"

sentences.zh: 」蕃欲求見詔書，范呵之曰：「卿非我故吏邪？

translations.literal: " Fan wished to see the edict. Fan shouted at him, "Are you not my former clerk?
translations.idiomatic: " Si Fan wished to see the edict. Fan shouted at him, "Are you not my former clerk?

sentences.zh: 何以敢爾！

translations.literal: How dare you act like this!"
translations.idiomatic: How dare you act like this!"

sentences.zh: 」乃開之。

translations.literal: " He then opened it.
translations.idiomatic: " He then opened it.

sentences.zh: 范出城，顧謂蕃曰：「太傅圖逆，卿從我去！

translations.literal: Fan left the city and, looking back, said to Fan, "The Grand Tutor plots rebellion—follow me!"
translations.idiomatic: Fan left the city and, looking back, said to Si Fan, "The Grand Tutor plots rebellion—follow me!"

sentences.zh: 」蕃徒行不能及，遂避側。

translations.literal: " Si Fan on foot could not keep up and so hid to one side.
translations.idiomatic: " Si Fan on foot could not keep up and hid to one side.

sentences.zh: 懿謂蔣濟曰：「智囊往矣！

translations.literal: Yi said to Jiang Ji, "The wisdom-bag has gone!"
translations.idiomatic: Yi said to Jiang Ji, "The wisdom-bag has gone!"

sentences.zh: 」濟曰：「范則智矣，然駑馬戀棧豆，爽必不能用也。

translations.literal: " Ji said, "Fan is wise, but a nag loves its manger and beans—Shuang will surely not use him."
translations.idiomatic: " Jiang Ji said, "Fan is wise, but a nag loves its manger—Shuang will surely not use him."

sentences.zh: 范至，勸爽兄弟以天子詣許昌，發四方兵以自輔。

translations.literal: When Fan arrived, he urged the Shuang brothers to take the Son of Heaven to Xuchang and raise troops from the four quarters to support themselves.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan arrived, he urged the Shuang brothers to take the emperor to Xuchang and raise troops from the four quarters to support themselves.

sentences.zh: 爽疑未決，范謂羲曰：「此事昭然，卿用讀書何為邪！

translations.literal: Shuang hesitated and could not decide. Fan said to Xi, "This matter is plain as day—what use were all your books!
translations.idiomatic: Shuang hesitated and could not decide. Fan said to Xi, "This matter is plain as day—what use were all your books!

sentences.zh: 於今日卿等門戶，求貧賤復可得乎！

translations.literal: From today on your house and gate—could you even seek poverty and baseness again!
translations.idiomatic: From today on could your house even seek poverty again!

sentences.zh: 且匹夫質一人，尚慾望活；

translations.literal: Moreover, a common man who holds one person hostage still hopes to live;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, a common man who holds one hostage still hopes to live;

sentences.zh: 卿與天子相隨，令於天下，誰敢不應也！

translations.literal: you follow the Son of Heaven and command the realm—who would dare not respond!"
translations.idiomatic: you follow the emperor and command the realm—who would dare not respond!"

sentences.zh: 」俱不言。

translations.literal: " All were silent.
translations.idiomatic: " All were silent.

sentences.zh: 范又謂羲曰：「卿別營近在闕南，洛陽典農治在城外，呼召如意。

translations.literal: Fan again said to Xi, "Your separate camp is near south of the palace gate; the Luoyang Director of Agriculture's office is outside the walls—summon them as you wish.
translations.idiomatic: Fan again said to Xi, "Your separate camp is near south of the palace gate; the Luoyang Director of Agriculture's office is outside the walls—summon them as you wish.

sentences.zh: 今詣許昌，不過中宿，許昌別庫，足相被假；

translations.literal: Going now to Xuchang, it is no more than an overnight stop; Xuchang's separate storehouses are sufficient to supply you;
translations.idiomatic: Going now to Xuchang is no more than an overnight stop; Xuchang's storehouses are sufficient to supply you;

sentences.zh: 所憂當在谷食，而大司農印章在我身。

translations.literal: what should be worried over is grain food—and the Grand Minister of Agriculture's seal is on my person."
translations.idiomatic: what should be worried over is grain—and the Grand Minister of Agriculture's seal is on my person."

sentences.zh: 」羲兄弟默然不從，自甲夜至五鼓，爽乃投刀於地曰：「我亦不失作富家翁！

translations.literal: " The Xi brothers were silent and would not follow. From the first watch of the night until the fifth drum, Shuang at last cast his sword to the ground and said, "I shall still not fail to be a rich household's elder!"
translations.idiomatic: " The Xi brothers were silent and would not follow. From the first watch until the fifth drum, Shuang at last cast his sword to the ground and said, "I shall still not fail to die a rich man!"

sentences.zh: 」范哭曰：「曹子丹佳人，生汝兄弟，犬屯犢耳！

translations.literal: " Fan wept and said, "Cao Zhen was a fine man—he fathered you brothers, a kennel of dogs and calves!
translations.idiomatic: " Fan wept and said, "Cao Zhen was a fine man—he fathered you brothers, a kennel of dogs and calves!

sentences.zh: 何圖今日坐汝等族滅也！

translations.literal: Who would have thought that today I should sit by and see your clan exterminated!"
translations.idiomatic: Who would have thought that today I should see your clan exterminated!"

sentences.zh: 爽乃通懿奏事，白帝下詔免己官，奉帝還宮。

translations.literal: Shuang then got through Yi's memorial, told the emperor to issue an edict dismissing his own office, and escorted the emperor back to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang then got through Yi's memorial, had the emperor issue an edict dismissing his own office, and escorted the emperor back to the palace.

sentences.zh: 爽兄弟歸家，懿發洛陽吏卒圍守之；

translations.literal: The Shuang brothers returned home; Yi dispatched Luoyang clerks and soldiers to surround and guard them;
translations.idiomatic: The Shuang brothers returned home, and Sima Yi dispatched Luoyang clerks and soldiers to surround and guard them;

sentences.zh: 四角作高樓，令人在樓上察視爽兄弟舉動。

translations.literal: At the four corners they built tall towers and posted men on the towers to observe the Shuang brothers' movements.
translations.idiomatic: At the four corners they built tall towers and posted men on them to watch the Shuang brothers' every move.

sentences.zh: 爽挾彈到後園中，樓上便唱言：「故大將軍東南行！

translations.literal: Shuang, pellet bow in hand, went to the rear garden; from the tower at once came a shout: "The former Grand General is heading southeast!
translations.idiomatic: Shuang went to the rear garden with his pellet bow; from the tower at once came a shout: "The former Grand General is heading southeast!

sentences.zh: 」爽愁悶不知為計。

translations.literal: " Shuang was distressed and depressed, not knowing what plan to adopt.
translations.idiomatic: " Shuang was anguished and depressed, not knowing what to do.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，有司奏：「黃門張當私以所擇才人與爽，疑有奸。

translations.literal: On the wuxu day, the relevant offices reported: "Yellow Gate Zhang Dang privately gave selected talented women to Shuang—suspected of improper relations.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuxu day, the relevant offices reported: "Yellow Gate Zhang Dang had privately given selected palace women to Shuang, and improper relations were suspected.

sentences.zh: 」收當付廷尉考實，辭云：「爽與尚書何晏、鄧颺、丁謐、司隸校尉畢軌、荊州刺史李勝等陰謀反逆，須三月中發。

translations.literal: " Zhang Dang was taken and handed to the Minister of Justice for examination; his testimony said: "Shuang, together with Masters of Writing He Yan, Deng Yang, and Ding Mi, Director of Retainers Bi Gui, and Inspector of Jing Province Li Sheng and others, secretly plotted rebellion, to be launched in the third month.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang Dang was arrested and handed to the Minister of Justice for interrogation; he testified that Shuang, together with Masters of Writing He Yan, Deng Yang, and Ding Mi, Director of Retainers Bi Gui, and Inspector of Jing Province Li Sheng and others, had secretly plotted rebellion to be launched in the third month.

sentences.zh: 」於是收爽、羲、訓、晏、颺、謐、軌、勝並桓范皆下獄，劾以大逆不道，與張當俱夷三族。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Shuang, Xi, Xun, Yan, Yang, Mi, Gui, Sheng, and Huan Fan were all taken into prison; charged with great treason and unnatural conduct, together with Zhang Dang their three clans were exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon Shuang, Xi, Xun, Yan, Yang, Mi, Gui, Sheng, and Huan Fan were all imprisoned; charged with great treason, they and Zhang Dang had their three clans exterminated.

sentences.zh: 初，爽之出也，司馬魯芝留在府，聞有變，將營騎斫津門出赴爽。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Shuang set out, Major Lu Zhi remained at headquarters; hearing of the coup, he was about to lead the camp cavalry to cut through the ferry gate and go to Shuang's aid.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Shuang set out, Major Lu Zhi had remained at headquarters; hearing of the coup, he was about to lead the camp cavalry through the ferry gate to join Shuang.

sentences.zh: 及爽解印綬，將出，主簿楊綜止之曰：「公挾主握權，捨此以至東市乎？

translations.literal: When Shuang removed his seal and cord and was about to leave, Chief Clerk Yang Zong stopped him, saying: "You held the ruler and grasped power—will you abandon this only to reach the Eastern Market?
translations.idiomatic: When Shuang removed his seal and cord and was about to leave, Chief Clerk Yang Zong stopped him, saying: "You held the emperor and wielded power—will you abandon all this only to end up at the Eastern Market?

sentences.zh: 」有司奏收芝、綜治罪，太傅懿曰：「彼各為其主也。

translations.literal: " The relevant offices memorialized to arrest Lu Zhi and Yang Zong for punishment; Grand Tutor Yi said: "Each was serving his own master.
translations.idiomatic: " The relevant offices memorialized to arrest Lu Zhi and Yang Zong for punishment; Grand Tutor Sima Yi said: "Each was serving his own master.

sentences.zh: 宥之。

translations.literal: Pardon them.
translations.idiomatic: Pardon them.

sentences.zh: 」頃之，以芝為御史中丞，綜為尚書郎。

translations.literal: " Before long, Lu Zhi was made Palace Censor, and Yang Zong was made Master of Writing Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long, Lu Zhi was appointed Palace Censor, and Yang Zong was appointed Master of Writing Attendant.

sentences.zh: 魯芝將出，呼參軍辛敞欲與俱去。

translations.literal: As Lu Zhi was about to go out, he called Staff Officer Xin Chang, wanting to go together.
translations.idiomatic: As Lu Zhi was about to go out, he called Staff Officer Xin Chang and wanted to go with him.

sentences.zh: 敞，毘之子也，其姊憲英為太常羊耽妻，敞與之謀曰：「天子在外，太傅閉城門，人云將不利國家，於事可得爾乎？

translations.literal: Chang was the son of Pi; his elder sister Xianying was wife of Grand Minister of Ceremonies Yang Dan. Chang consulted with her, saying: "The Son of Heaven is outside; the Grand Tutor has closed the city gates—people say he intends harm to the state; can that really be so in the affair?
translations.idiomatic: Chang was the son of Pi; his elder sister Xianying was the wife of Grand Minister of Ceremonies Yang Dan. Chang consulted with her, saying: "The emperor is outside the city, and the Grand Tutor has closed the gates—people say he intends harm to the state; can that really be so?

sentences.zh: 」憲英曰：「以吾度之，太傅此舉，不過以誅曹爽耳。

translations.literal: " Xianying said: "By my estimate, the Grand Tutor's move is nothing more than to execute Cao Shuang.
translations.idiomatic: " Xianying said: "By my estimate, the Grand Tutor's move is nothing more than to execute Cao Shuang.

sentences.zh: 」敞曰：「然則事就乎？

translations.literal: " Chang said: "Then will the affair succeed?
translations.idiomatic: " Chang said: "Then will it succeed?

sentences.zh: 」憲英曰：「得無殆就！

translations.literal: " Xianying said: "Probably almost certainly!
translations.idiomatic: " Xianying said: "Almost certainly!

sentences.zh: 爽之才非太傅之偶也。

translations.literal: Shuang's talent is no match for the Grand Tutor's.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang's talent is no match for the Grand Tutor's.

sentences.zh: 」敞曰：「然則敞可以無出乎？

translations.literal: " Chang said: "Then may Chang stay and not go out?
translations.idiomatic: " Chang said: "Then may I stay and not go out?

sentences.zh: 」憲英曰：「安可以不出！

translations.literal: " Xianying said: "How can you not go out!
translations.idiomatic: " Xianying said: "How can you not go out!

sentences.zh: 職守，人之大義也。

translations.literal: Duty—that is humanity's great principle.
translations.idiomatic: Duty is humanity's greatest principle.

sentences.zh: 凡人在難，猶或恤之；

translations.literal: When anyone is in difficulty, one may still pity him;
translations.idiomatic: When anyone is in difficulty, one may still pity him;

sentences.zh: 為人執鞭而棄其事，不祥莫大焉。

translations.literal: to take another's whip yet abandon one's task—no ill omen could be greater.
translations.idiomatic: to take another's whip yet abandon one's post—no ill omen could be greater.

sentences.zh: 且為人任，為人死，親暱之職也，從眾而已。

translations.literal: Moreover, to be employed by someone is to die for someone—that is the duty of the intimate retainer; one simply follows the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, to be employed by someone is to die for someone—that is the duty of a close retainer; one simply follows the crowd.

sentences.zh: 」敞遂出。

translations.literal: " Chang then went out.
translations.idiomatic: " Chang then went out.

sentences.zh: 事定之後，敞歎曰：「吾不謀於姊，幾不獲於義。

translations.literal: After matters were settled, Chang sighed and said: "Had I not consulted my elder sister, I would nearly have failed to obtain righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: After matters were settled, Chang sighed and said: "Had I not consulted my elder sister, I would nearly have failed to do what was right.

sentences.zh: 先是，爽辟王沈及太山羊祜，沈勸祜應命。

translations.literal: Earlier, Shuang had recruited Wang Shen and Yang Hu of Taishan; Shen urged Hu to accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Shuang had recruited Wang Shen and Yang Hu of Taishan; Shen urged Hu to accept the appointment.

sentences.zh: 祜曰：「委質事人，復何容易！

translations.literal: Hu said: "To entrust one's person and serve another—how can that be so easy!
translations.idiomatic: Hu said: "To pledge oneself and serve another—how can that be taken lightly!

sentences.zh: 」沈遂行。

translations.literal: " Shen then went.
translations.idiomatic: " Shen then went.

sentences.zh: 及爽敗，沈以故吏免，乃謂祜曰：「吾不忘卿前語。

translations.literal: When Shuang was defeated, Shen was dismissed as a former subordinate; he then said to Hu: "I have not forgotten your earlier words.
translations.idiomatic: When Shuang was defeated, Shen was dismissed as a former subordinate; he then said to Hu: "I have not forgotten what you said before.

sentences.zh: 」祜曰：「此非始慮所及也！

translations.literal: " Hu said: "That was not what I foresaw at the start!
translations.idiomatic: " Hu said: "That was not what I had foreseen at the outset!

sentences.zh: 爽從弟文叔妻夏侯令女，早寡而無子，其父文寧欲嫁之；

translations.literal: Shuang's younger cousin Wenshu's wife was Lady Xiahou Lingnü; widowed early without a son, her father Wenning wished to marry her off again;
translations.idiomatic: The wife of Shuang's younger cousin Wenshu was Lady Xiahou Lingnü; widowed early and childless, her father Wenning wished to marry her off again;

sentences.zh: 令女刀截兩耳以自誓，居常依爽。

translations.literal: Lady Lingnü cut off both ears with a knife to bind herself by oath, and ordinarily relied on Shuang.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Lingnü cut off both ears with a knife to bind herself by oath and ordinarily relied on Shuang.

sentences.zh: 爽誅，其家上書絕昏，強迎以歸，復將嫁之；

translations.literal: When Shuang was executed, her family submitted a memorial severing the marriage, forcibly took her home, and again wished to marry her off;
translations.idiomatic: When Shuang was executed, her family submitted a memorial severing the marriage, forcibly brought her home, and again wished to marry her off;

sentences.zh: 令女竊入寢室，引刀自斷其鼻，其家驚惋，謂之曰：「人生世間，如輕塵棲弱草耳，何至自苦乃爾！

translations.literal: Lady Lingnü stole into the bedchamber, drew a knife and cut off her nose; her family was shocked and grieved, and said to her: "Life in this world is like light dust resting on frail grass—why torment yourself to such a degree!
translations.idiomatic: Lady Lingnü stole into the bedchamber and cut off her nose with a knife; her family was shocked and grieved, and said to her: "Life in this world is like light dust resting on frail grass—why torment yourself so!

sentences.zh: 且夫家夷滅已盡，守此欲誰為哉！

translations.literal: Moreover, your husband's house has been exterminated to the last man—for whom do you keep this!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, your husband's house has been exterminated to the last man—for whom do you keep this!

sentences.zh: 」令女曰：「吾聞仁者不以盛衰改節，義者不以存亡易心。

translations.literal: " Lady Lingnü said: "I have heard that the benevolent do not change their integrity according to rise or decline, and the righteous do not alter their heart according to survival or destruction.
translations.idiomatic: " Lady Lingnü said: "I have heard that the benevolent do not change their integrity with rise or decline, and the righteous do not alter their hearts with survival or destruction.

sentences.zh: 曹氏前盛之時，尚欲保終，況今衰亡，何忍棄之！

translations.literal: When the Cao house was formerly flourishing, I still wished to preserve my marriage to the end—how much less now in decline and ruin could I bear to abandon it!
translations.idiomatic: When the Cao house was at its height, I still wished to preserve my marriage to the end—how much less now, in decline and ruin, could I bear to abandon it!

sentences.zh: 此禽獸不行，吾豈為乎！

translations.literal: Beasts would not do this—how could I!
translations.idiomatic: Even beasts would not do this—how could I!

sentences.zh: 」司馬懿聞而賢之，聽使乞子字養為曹氏後。

translations.literal: " Sima Yi heard and esteemed her, and permitted her to adopt a son to raise as heir of the Cao line.
translations.idiomatic: " Sima Yi heard of this and admired her, and permitted her to adopt a son to raise as heir of the Cao line.

sentences.zh: 何晏等方用事，自以為一時才傑，人莫能及。

translations.literal: He Yan and the others were then in power; they regarded themselves as geniuses of the age whom no one could match.
translations.idiomatic: He Yan and his circle were then in power; they regarded themselves as the geniuses of the age, unmatched by anyone.

sentences.zh: 晏嘗為名士品目曰：「唯深也故能通天下之志，夏侯泰初是也。

translations.literal: Yan once ranked the celebrated men, saying: "Only depth can penetrate the will of all under Heaven—Xiahou Taichu is such a one.
translations.idiomatic: He Yan once ranked the celebrated men of the age, saying: "Only depth can penetrate the will of all under Heaven—Xiahou Taichu is such a man.

sentences.zh: 唯幾也故能成天下之務，司馬子元是也。

translations.literal: Only subtle insight can accomplish the affairs of all under Heaven—Sima Ziyuan is such a one.
translations.idiomatic: Only subtle insight can accomplish the affairs of all under Heaven—Sima Ziyuan is such a man.

sentences.zh: 唯神也不疾而速，不行而至，吾聞其語，未同凶其人。

translations.literal: Only spirit achieves speed without haste and arrival without going—I have heard that saying but have not yet met the man, and already detest him.
translations.idiomatic: Only spirit achieves speed without haste and arrival without travel—I have heard that saying but have not yet met the man, and already detest him.

sentences.zh: 」蓋欲以神況諸己也。

translations.literal: " He probably wished to compare the quality of "spirit" to himself.
translations.idiomatic: " He probably wished to compare the quality of "spirit" to himself.

sentences.zh: 選部郎劉陶，曄之子也，少有口辯，鄧颺之徒稱之以為伊、呂。

translations.literal: Selection Department Attendant Liu Tao, son of Ye, was eloquent from youth; Deng Yang and his ilk praised him as an Yi Yin or Lü Shang.
translations.idiomatic: Selection Department Attendant Liu Tao, son of Liu Ye, was eloquent from youth; Deng Yang and his circle praised him as an Yi Yin or Lü Shang.

sentences.zh: 陶嘗謂傅玄是「仲尼不聖。

translations.literal: Tao once said of Fu Xuan: "Confucius was not a sage.
translations.idiomatic: Tao once said of Fu Xuan: "Confucius was not a sage.

sentences.zh: 何以知之？

translations.literal: How does one know?
translations.idiomatic: How does one know?

sentences.zh: 智者於群愚，如弄一丸於掌中；

translations.literal: The wise man among the mass of fools is like rolling a single pellet in the palm;
translations.idiomatic: The wise man among the mass of fools is like rolling a single pellet in the palm of one's hand;

sentences.zh: 而不能得天下，何以為聖！

translations.literal: yet he could not obtain all under Heaven—how can he be called a sage!
translations.idiomatic: yet he could not obtain all under Heaven—how can he be called a sage!

sentences.zh: 」玄不復難，但語之曰：「天下之變無常也，今見卿窮。

translations.literal: " Xuan did not argue further, but only said to him: "Changes under Heaven are without constancy; today I see you in straits.
translations.idiomatic: " Fu Xuan did not argue further, but only said to him: "Fortunes under Heaven are never constant; today I see you in straits.

sentences.zh: 」及曹爽敗，陶退居裡捨，乃謝其言之過。

translations.literal: " When Cao Shuang was defeated, Tao retired to his neighborhood and apologized for the excess of his words.
translations.idiomatic: " When Cao Shuang was defeated, Tao retired to his neighborhood and apologized for the excess of his words.

sentences.zh: 管輅之舅謂輅曰：「爾前何以知何、鄧之敗？

translations.literal: Guan Lu's maternal uncle said to Lu: "How did you earlier know of the defeat of He and Deng?
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu's maternal uncle said to him: "How did you know beforehand that He Yan and Deng Yang would fall?

sentences.zh: 」輅曰：「鄧之行步，筋不束骨，脈不制肉，起立傾倚，若無手足，此為鬼躁。

translations.literal: " Lu said: "When Deng walked, his sinews did not bind his bones, his pulses did not control his flesh; standing up he leaned and swayed as if without hands or feet—this is 'restless ghost.'
translations.idiomatic: " Guan Lu said: "When Deng Yang walked, his sinews did not bind his bones and his pulses did not control his flesh; when he stood he leaned and swayed as if he had no hands or feet—this is 'restless ghost.'

sentences.zh: 何之視候則魂不守宅，血不華色，精爽煙浮，容若槁木，此為鬼幽。

translations.literal: When He observed and looked about, his soul did not keep to its dwelling, his blood did not color his face, his vital spirit floated like smoke, his countenance like dry wood—this is 'dark ghost.'
translations.idiomatic: When He Yan looked about, his soul did not keep to its dwelling, his blood did not color his face, his vital spirit floated like smoke, and his countenance was like dry wood—this is 'dark ghost.'

sentences.zh: 二者皆非遐福之象也。

translations.literal: Neither is a sign of distant blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Neither is a sign of lasting good fortune.

sentences.zh: 何晏性自喜，粉白不去手，行步顧影。

translations.literal: He Yan by nature greatly delighted in himself; white powder never left his hand, and as he walked he looked back at his shadow.
translations.idiomatic: He Yan by nature greatly delighted in himself; white powder never left his hand, and as he walked he looked back at his shadow.

sentences.zh: 尤好老、莊之書，與夏侯玄、荀粲及山陽王弼之徒，競為清談，祖尚虛無，謂《六經》為聖人糟粕。

translations.literal: He especially favored the books of Laozi and Zhuangzi; with Xiahou Xuan, Xun Can, and Wang Bi of Shanyang and others he vied in pure talk, esteeming emptiness and nothingness, calling the Six Classics the dregs left by sages.
translations.idiomatic: He especially favored the books of Laozi and Zhuangzi; with Xiahou Xuan, Xun Can, Wang Bi of Shanyang, and others he vied in pure talk, esteeming emptiness and nothingness and calling the Six Classics the dregs left by sages.

sentences.zh: 由是天下士大夫爭慕效之，遂成風流，不可複製焉。

translations.literal: From this the literati and officials of all under Heaven competed to emulate them, until it became a fashion that could never be duplicated.
translations.idiomatic: From this the literati and officials throughout the realm competed to emulate them, until it became a fashion beyond replication.

sentences.zh: 粲，彧之子也。

translations.literal: Can was the son of Yu.
