translations.idiomatic: Xun Can was the son of Xun Yu.

sentences.zh: 丙午，大赦。

translations.literal: On the bingwu day, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingwu day, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 丁未，以太傅懿為丞相，加九錫，懿固辭不受。

translations.literal: On the dingwei day, Grand Tutor Yi was made Chancellor and granted the Nine Bestowments; Yi firmly declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingwei day, Grand Tutor Sima Yi was made Chancellor and granted the Nine Bestowments; Sima Yi firmly declined and would not accept.

sentences.zh: 初，右將軍夏侯霸為曹爽所厚，以其父淵死於蜀，常切齒有報仇之志，為討蜀護軍，屯於隴西，統屬征西。

translations.literal: Earlier, General of the Right Xiahou Ba had been treated generously by Cao Shuang; because his father Yuan had died in Shu, he constantly gnashed his teeth with a will to avenge, served as Protector of the Army for the Campaign against Shu, and was stationed in Longxi under the command of the Campaign-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, General of the Right Xiahou Ba had been treated generously by Cao Shuang; because his father Yuan had died in Shu, he constantly gnashed his teeth with a will to avenge, served as Protector of the Army for the Campaign against Shu, and was stationed in Longxi under the Campaign-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 征西將軍夏侯玄，霸之從子，爽之外弟也。

translations.literal: Campaign-in-Chief of the West Xiahou Xuan was Ba's nephew and Shuang's maternal younger cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Campaign-in-Chief of the West Xiahou Xuan was Ba's nephew and Cao Shuang's maternal younger cousin.

sentences.zh: 爽既誅，司馬懿召玄詣京師，以雍州刺史郭淮代之。

translations.literal: After Shuang was executed, Sima Yi summoned Xuan to the capital and replaced him with Inspector of Yong Province Guo Huai.
translations.idiomatic: After Cao Shuang was executed, Sima Yi summoned Xuan to the capital and replaced him with Inspector of Yong Province Guo Huai.

sentences.zh: 霸素與淮不葉，以為禍必相及，大懼，遂奔漢。

translations.literal: Ba had long been at odds with Huai; he believed disaster was sure to reach him as well, was greatly afraid, and fled to Han.
translations.idiomatic: Ba had long been at odds with Guo Huai; believing disaster was sure to reach him as well, he was greatly afraid and fled to Shu Han.

sentences.zh: 漢主謂曰：「卿父自遇害於行間耳，非我先人之手刃也。

translations.literal: The Han ruler said to him: "Your father was himself slain on the battlefield—it was not my forebear's hand that cut him down personally.
translations.idiomatic: The Han ruler said to him: "Your father was slain on the battlefield—it was not my forebear who personally cut him down.

sentences.zh: 」遇之甚厚。

translations.literal: " He treated him with great kindness.
translations.idiomatic: " He treated him with great kindness.

sentences.zh: 姜維問於霸曰：「司馬懿既得彼政，當復有征伐之志不？

translations.literal: Jiang Wei asked Ba: "Now that Sima Yi has grasped power there, will he again have the will to campaign and conquer?
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei asked Ba: "Now that Sima Yi has seized power there, will he again have the will to campaign and conquer?

sentences.zh: 」霸曰：「彼方營立家門，未遑外事。

translations.literal: " Ba said: "They are just now busy establishing their house—they have no leisure for outside affairs.
translations.idiomatic: " Ba said: "They are just now busy establishing their house and have no leisure for outside affairs.

sentences.zh: 有鐘士季者，其人雖少，若管朝政，吳、蜀之憂也。

translations.literal: There is a Zhong Shiji; though the man is young, if he comes to manage court affairs, he will be Wu's and Shu's worry.
translations.idiomatic: There is a Zhong Shiji; though the man is young, if he comes to manage court affairs, he will be the worry of Wu and Shu.

sentences.zh: 」士季者，鐘繇之子尚書郎會也。

translations.literal: " Shiji was Attendant of the Masters of Writing Zhong Hui, son of Zhong Yao.
translations.idiomatic: " Shiji was Attendant of the Masters of Writing Zhong Hui, son of Zhong Yao.

sentences.zh: 三月，吳左大司馬朱然卒。

translations.literal: In the third month, Left Grand Marshal of Wu Zhu Ran died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Left Grand Marshal of Wu Zhu Ran died.

sentences.zh: 然長不盈七尺，氣候分明，內行修潔，終日欽欽，常若在戰場，臨急膽定，過絕於人。

translations.literal: Ran was not quite seven feet tall; his bearing was clear and distinct, his inner conduct cultivated and pure; all day he was reverently attentive, always as if on a battlefield; facing peril his courage was steady, surpassing others.
translations.idiomatic: Ran was not quite seven feet tall; his bearing was clear and distinct and his inner conduct cultivated and pure. All day he was reverently attentive, always as if on a battlefield; facing peril his courage was steady and surpassed others.

sentences.zh: 雖世無事，每朝夕嚴鼓，兵在營者，鹹行裝就隊。

translations.literal: Though the age was without warfare, morning and evening he sounded the war drums; soldiers in camp all donned gear and took their places.
translations.idiomatic: Though the realm was at peace, morning and evening he sounded the war drums, and soldiers in camp all donned gear and took their places.

sentences.zh: 以此玩敵，使不知所備，故出輒有功。

translations.literal: By this he wearied the enemy and kept them from knowing his preparations; hence whenever he went out he achieved merit.
translations.idiomatic: By this he wearied the enemy and kept them from knowing his preparations, so whenever he went out he achieved merit.

sentences.zh: 然寢疾增篤，吳主晝為減膳，夜為不寐，中使醫藥口食之物，相望於道。

translations.literal: When Ran's illness grew severe, the Lord of Wu by day reduced his meals and by night could not sleep; palace messengers with medicine and food filled the road.
translations.idiomatic: When Ran's illness grew severe, the Lord of Wu reduced his meals by day and could not sleep by night; palace messengers bearing medicine and food filled the road.

sentences.zh: 然每遣使表疾病消息，吳主輒召見，口自問訊，入賜酒食，出賜布帛。

translations.literal: Whenever Ran sent an envoy reporting on his illness, the Lord of Wu at once summoned him, personally questioned him by mouth, gave wine and food on entering and cloth and silk on leaving.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Ran sent an envoy reporting on his illness, the Lord of Wu at once summoned him, questioned him in person, gave wine and food when he entered, and cloth and silk when he left.

sentences.zh: 及卒，吳主為之哀慟。

translations.literal: When he died, the Lord of Wu mourned for him with anguish.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, the Lord of Wu mourned for him with anguish.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，乙丑，改元。

translations.literal: In summer, fourth month, on the yichou day, the reign title was changed.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, on the yichou day, the reign title was changed.

sentences.zh: 曹爽之在伊南也，昌陵景侯蔣濟與之書，言太傅之旨，不過免官而已。

translations.literal: When Cao Shuang was at Yinan, Marquis Jing of Changling Jiang Ji wrote him a letter saying the Grand Tutor's intent was no more than dismissal from office.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Shuang was at Yinan, Marquis Jing of Changling Jiang Ji wrote him a letter saying the Grand Tutor's intent was no more than dismissal from office.

sentences.zh: 爽誅，濟進封都鄉侯，上疏固辭，不許。

translations.literal: After Shuang was executed, Ji was advanced in enfeoffment to Marquis of Duxiang; he submitted a memorial firmly declining, but it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: After Shuang was executed, Jiang Ji was advanced in enfeoffment to Marquis of Duxiang; he submitted a memorial firmly declining, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 濟病其言之失，遂發病，丙子，卒。

translations.literal: Ji was troubled by the failure of his words and fell ill; on the bingzi day he died.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was troubled by the failure of his words and fell ill; on the bingzi day he died.

sentences.zh: 秋，漢衛將軍姜維寇雍州，依麴山築二城，使牙門將句安、李歆等守之，聚羌胡質任，侵逼諸郡。

translations.literal: In autumn, General of the Guard Jiang Wei of Han raided Yong Province, built two cities relying on Mount Qu, and had Gate Officer Gou An, Li Xin, and others guard them, gathering Qiang and Hu hostages and pressing upon the commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, General of the Guard Jiang Wei of Han raided Yong Province, built two cities on Mount Qu, and had Gate Officers Gou An and Li Xin and others guard them, gathering Qiang and Hu hostages and pressing upon the commanderies.

sentences.zh: 征西將軍郭淮與雍州刺史陳泰御之。

translations.literal: Campaign-in-Chief of the West Guo Huai and Inspector of Yong Province Chen Tai resisted them.
translations.idiomatic: Campaign-in-Chief of the West Guo Huai and Inspector of Yong Province Chen Tai resisted them.

sentences.zh: 泰曰：「麴城雖固，去蜀險遠，當須運糧；

translations.literal: Tai said: "Though Qu cities are strong, they are far from Shu through dangerous terrain and must rely on transporting grain;
translations.idiomatic: Chen Tai said: "Though the Qu cities are strong, they are far from Shu through dangerous terrain and must rely on transporting grain;

sentences.zh: 羌夷患維勞役，必未肯附。

translations.literal: the Qiang and barbarians will resent Wei's forced labor and surely will not be willing to attach themselves.
translations.idiomatic: the Qiang and barbarians will resent Jiang Wei's forced labor and surely will not be willing to submit.

sentences.zh: 今圍而取之，可不血刃而拔其城；

translations.literal: If we surround and take them now, we can capture the cities without bloodshed;
translations.idiomatic: If we surround and take them now, we can capture the cities without bloodshed;

sentences.zh: 雖其有救，山道阻險，非行兵之地也。

translations.literal: even if they have rescue, the mountain roads are dangerous and narrow—not ground for marching troops."
translations.idiomatic: even if they send relief, the mountain roads are dangerous and narrow—not ground for marching troops."

sentences.zh: 」淮乃使泰率討蜀護軍徐質、南安太守鄧艾進兵圍麴城，斷其運道及城外流水。

translations.literal: " Huai then had Tai lead Protector of the Army for the Campaign against Shu Xu Zhi and Administrator of Nan'an Deng Ai to advance and besiege Qu city, cutting off its supply route and the water flowing outside the walls.
translations.idiomatic: " Guo Huai then had Chen Tai lead Protector of the Army for the Campaign against Shu Xu Zhi and Administrator of Nan'an Deng Ai to advance and besiege Qu city, cutting off its supply route and the water flowing outside the walls.

sentences.zh: 安等挑戰，不許，將士困窘，分糧聚雪以引日月。

translations.literal: An and the others offered battle but were not accepted; officers and soldiers were distressed, rationing grain and gathering snow to prolong their days.
translations.idiomatic: Gou An and the others offered battle but were refused; officers and soldiers were in dire straits, rationing grain and gathering snow to prolong their days.

sentences.zh: 維引兵救之，出自牛頭山，與泰相對。

translations.literal: Wei led troops to rescue them, coming out from Mount Niutou, and faced Tai across from him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei led troops to rescue them, coming out from Mount Niutou, and faced Chen Tai across from him.

sentences.zh: 泰曰：「兵法貴在不戰而屈人。

translations.literal: Tai said: "The art of war values subduing men without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Tai said: "The art of war values subduing the enemy without fighting.

sentences.zh: 今絕牛頭，維無反道，則我之禽也。

translations.literal: Now cut off Niutou, and if Wei has no way back, he will be our captive.
translations.idiomatic: Now cut off Niutou, and if Jiang Wei has no way back, he will be our captive.

sentences.zh: 」敕諸軍各堅壘勿與戰，遣使白淮，使淮趣牛頭截其還路。

translations.literal: " He ordered the armies each to hold their ramparts and not give battle, and sent a messenger to report to Huai, telling Huai to hasten to Niutou and cut off Wei's return route.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered the armies each to hold their ramparts and not give battle, and sent a messenger to report to Guo Huai, telling him to hasten to Niutou and cut off Jiang Wei's return route.

sentences.zh: 淮從之，進軍洮水。

translations.literal: Huai followed this, advancing his army to the Tao River.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Huai followed this plan and advanced his army to the Tao River.

sentences.zh: 維懼，遁走，安等孤絕，遂降。

translations.literal: Wei was afraid and fled; An and the others were isolated and cut off, and thereupon surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei was afraid and fled; Gou An and the others were isolated and cut off, and thereupon surrendered.

sentences.zh: 淮因西擊諸羌。

translations.literal: Huai thereupon struck west against the various Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Huai thereupon marched west to attack the Qiang tribes.

sentences.zh: 鄧艾曰：「賊去未遠，或能復還，宜分諸軍以備不虞。

translations.literal: Deng Ai said: "The enemy has not gone far and may return; the armies should be divided to guard against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai said, "The enemy has not gone far and may yet return. We should divide our forces to guard against surprise.

sentences.zh: 」於是留艾屯白水北。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Ai was left encamped north of Baishui.
translations.idiomatic: " So Deng Ai was left encamped north of the Baishui River.

sentences.zh: 三日，維遣其將廖化自白水南向艾結營。

translations.literal: Three days later, Wei sent his general Liao Hua from south of Baishui toward Ai to set up camp.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later, Jiang Wei sent his general Liao Hua south from the Baishui River toward Deng Ai to establish a camp.

sentences.zh: 艾謂諸將曰：「維今卒還，吾軍人少，法當來渡；

translations.literal: Ai said to the generals: "Wei has suddenly returned; our army is few; by rule he ought to come to cross;
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai said to his generals, "Jiang Wei has suddenly returned. Our force is small; by ordinary tactics he ought to try to cross the river;

sentences.zh: 而不作橋，此維使化持吾令不得還，維必自東襲取洮城。

translations.literal: yet he builds no bridge—this means Wei has sent Hua to hold us so we cannot return; Wei will surely strike east himself to seize Taocheng.
translations.idiomatic: yet he builds no bridge. This means Jiang Wei has sent Liao Hua to pin us down so we cannot return, while he himself will surely strike east to seize Taocheng.

sentences.zh: 」洮城在水北，去艾屯六十里，艾即夜潛軍徑到。

translations.literal: " Taocheng was north of the water, sixty li from Ai's camp; Ai that very night secretly marched his army directly there.
translations.idiomatic: " Taocheng lay north of the river, sixty li from Deng Ai's camp. That very night he secretly marched his army straight there.

sentences.zh: 維果來渡，而艾先至據城，得以不敗，漢軍遂還。

translations.literal: Wei did indeed come to cross, but Ai arrived first and held the city, and so was not defeated; the Han army thereupon withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei did come to cross the river, but Deng Ai arrived first and held the city, and so was not defeated. The Han army then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 兗州刺史令狐愚，司空王凌之甥也，屯於平阿，甥舅並典重兵，專淮南之任。

translations.literal: Yanzhou Inspector Linghu Yu, nephew of Minister of Works Wang Ling, was encamped at Ping'a; nephew and uncle alike commanded great armies and held exclusive charge of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhou Inspector Linghu Yu, nephew of Minister of Works Wang Ling, was encamped at Ping'a. Nephew and uncle alike commanded major armies and held exclusive responsibility for Huainan.

sentences.zh: 凌與愚陰謀，以帝闇弱，制於強臣，聞楚王彪有智勇，欲共立之，迎都許昌。

translations.literal: Ling and Yu plotted in secret, reckoning the emperor dim and weak and controlled by powerful ministers; hearing that Prince of Chu Biao had wisdom and courage, they wished together to set him up and welcome the capital to Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ling and Linghu Yu plotted in secret. Reckoning the emperor weak and dim, controlled by powerful ministers, and hearing that Prince of Chu Cao Biao had wisdom and courage, they wished to set him up together and move the capital to Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 九月，愚遣其將張式至白馬，與楚王相聞。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Yu sent his general Zhang Shi to Baima to communicate with the Prince of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Linghu Yu sent his general Zhang Shi to Baima to establish contact with the Prince of Chu.

sentences.zh: 凌又遣舍人勞精詣洛陽，語其子廣。

translations.literal: Ling also sent house steward Lao Jing to Luoyang to speak with his son Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ling also sent house steward Lao Jing to Luoyang to speak with his son Wang Guang.

sentences.zh: 廣曰：「凡舉大事，應本人情。

translations.literal: Guang said: "Whenever one undertakes a great affair, one must accord with human sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guang said, "Whenever one undertakes a great affair, one must follow the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 曹爽以驕奢失民，何平叔虛華不治，丁、畢、桓、鄧雖並有宿望，皆專競於世。

translations.literal: Cao Shuang lost the people through arrogance and luxury; He Pingshu was empty brilliance without governance; Ding, Bi, Huan, and Deng, though all possessed longstanding repute, all contended exclusively in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Shuang lost the people through arrogance and extravagance. He Yan was all show and no governance. Ding, Bi, Huan, and Deng, though all men of longstanding repute, were obsessed with rivalry in their day.

sentences.zh: 加變易朝典，政令數改，所存雖高而事不下接，民習於舊，眾莫之從，故雖勢傾四海，聲震天下，同日斬戮，名士減半，而百姓安之。

translations.literal: Add to this that they changed court institutions and altered government orders repeatedly; though their station was lofty, affairs did not reach down to the people; the people were accustomed to the old ways and none followed them—thus though their power tilted the four seas and their fame shook the world, on the same day they were beheaded and half the celebrated men were cut down, yet the common people were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover they altered court institutions and changed government orders again and again. Though their station was lofty, their rule never reached the people below. The people clung to the old ways and would not follow them. Thus though their power tilted the four seas and their fame shook the world, they were beheaded on the same day, celebrated men cut down by half, yet the common people were at peace.

sentences.zh: 莫之或哀，失民故也。

translations.literal: None mourned them—because they had lost the people.
translations.idiomatic: None mourned them, because they had lost the people.

sentences.zh: 今司馬懿情雖難量，事未有逆，而擢用賢能，廣樹勝己，修先朝之政令，副眾心之所求。

translations.literal: Now Sima Yi's disposition, though hard to measure, shows no rebellion in his deeds; he promotes the worthy and able, widely employs men who surpass himself, restores the government orders of former dynasties, and matches what the multitude's hearts seek.
translations.idiomatic: Now Sima Yi's intentions, though hard to read, show no rebellion in his deeds. He promotes the worthy and able, widely employs men better than himself, restores the government orders of the former reign, and meets what the people desire.

sentences.zh: 爽之所以為惡者，彼莫不必改，夙夜菲懈，以恤民為先，父子兄弟，並握兵要，未易亡也。

translations.literal: Whatever Shuang did ill, Yi changes it all; he toils day and night without slackening, putting care for the people first; father, sons, and brothers together hold the keys to military power—not easily destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever Cao Shuang did wrong, Sima Yi changes it. He toils day and night without slackening, putting care for the people first. Father, sons, and brothers together hold the keys to military power. They will not easily be overthrown.

sentences.zh: 」凌不從。

translations.literal: " Ling would not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Ling would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，令狐愚復遣張式詣楚王，未還，會愚病卒。

translations.literal: Winter, eleventh month: Linghu Yu again sent Zhang Shi to the Prince of Chu; before he returned, Yu fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the eleventh month, Linghu Yu again sent Zhang Shi to the Prince of Chu. Before Zhang Shi returned, Yu fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 十二月，辛卿，即拜王凌為太尉。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, day Xinqing: Wang Ling was immediately appointed Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the day xinqing, Wang Ling was immediately appointed Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 庚子，以司隸校尉孫禮為司空。

translations.literal: On day Gengzi, Metropolitan Commandant Sun Li was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengzi, Metropolitan Commandant Sun Li was made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 光祿大夫徐邈卒。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Xu Miao died.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Xu Miao died.

sentences.zh: 邈以清節著名，盧欽嘗著書稱邈曰：「徐公志高行潔，才博氣猛，其施之也，高而不狷，潔而不介，博而守約，猛而能寬。

translations.literal: Miao was famed for purity of conduct. Lu Qin once wrote in a book praising Miao, saying, "Lord Xu's will was lofty and his conduct clean; his talent broad and his spirit fierce. In applying them, he was lofty yet not narrow, clean yet not brittle, broad yet keeping to essentials, fierce yet able to be lenient.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Miao was famed for purity of conduct. Lu Qin once wrote in praise of him, "Lord Xu's aspirations were lofty and his conduct pure; his talent was broad and his spirit bold. In applying them, he was lofty without being narrow, pure without being brittle, broad yet restrained, bold yet capable of mercy.

sentences.zh: 聖人以清為難，而徐公之所易也。

translations.literal: The sages find purity difficult—yet for Lord Xu it was easy.
translations.idiomatic: The sages find purity difficult, yet for Lord Xu it was easy.

sentences.zh: 」或問欽：「徐公當武帝之時，人以為通；

translations.literal: " Someone asked Qin: "When Lord Xu was under Emperor Wu, people regarded him as accommodating;
translations.idiomatic: " Someone asked Lu Qin, "When Lord Xu served under Emperor Wu, people considered him accommodating;

sentences.zh: 自為涼州刺史，及還京師，人以為介，何也？

translations.literal: yet after he became Inspector of Liangzhou and returned to the capital, people regarded him as rigid—why?"
translations.idiomatic: yet after he became Inspector of Liangzhou and returned to the capital, people considered him rigid. Why was that?"

sentences.zh: 」欽答曰：「往者毛孝先、崔季珪用事，貴清素之士，於時皆變易車服以求名高，而徐公不改其常，故人以為通。

translations.literal: " Qin answered: "In the past when Mao Xiaoxian and Cui Jigui held power, they valued men of purity and simplicity; at the time all changed carriages and dress to seek fame, but Lord Xu did not alter his usual ways, so people regarded him as accommodating.
translations.idiomatic: " Lu Qin answered, "In the past when Mao Zeng and Cui Yan held power, they valued men of plain austerity. At the time everyone changed carriages and dress to win renown, but Lord Xu did not alter his ways, so people considered him accommodating.

sentences.zh: 比來天下奢靡，轉相倣傚，而徐公雅尚自若，不與俗同，故前日之通，乃今日之介也。

translations.literal: Recently the realm has grown luxurious and men copy one another in turn, yet Lord Xu holds to elegance as before and does not follow the common fashion—thus what was accommodation yesterday is rigidity today.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the realm has grown luxurious and men copy one another in turn, yet Lord Xu holds to his own refined standards and does not follow the crowd. Thus what was accommodation yesterday is rigidity today.

sentences.zh: 是世人之無常而徐公之有常也。

translations.literal: It is that the world's people are inconstant while Lord Xu is constant.
translations.idiomatic: The world's people are inconstant; Lord Xu alone is constant.

sentences.zh: 」欽，毓之子也。

translations.literal: " Qin was the son of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: " Lu Qin was the son of Lu Yu.

sentences.zh: 邵陵厲公中嘉平二年（

translations.literal: Deposed Emperor of Shaoling, Jiaping year two (
translations.idiomatic: Deposed Emperor of Shaoling, Jiaping year 2 (

sentences.zh: 庚午，公元二五零年）

translations.literal: Gengwu, the year 250 of the Common Era)
translations.idiomatic: gengwu cycle, AD 250)

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，以征西將軍郭淮為車騎將軍。

translations.literal: Summer, fifth month: Campaign-in-Chief of the West Guo Huai was made General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fifth month, Campaign-in-Chief of the West Guo Huai was made General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 初，會稽潘夫人有寵於吳主，生少子亮，吳主愛之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Lady Pan of Kuaiji enjoyed favor with Wu's ruler and bore his youngest son Liang; the ruler loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Lady Pan of Kuaiji enjoyed favor with Sun Quan and bore his youngest son Sun Liang, whom the ruler loved.

sentences.zh: 全公主既與太子和有隙，欲豫自結，數稱亮美，以其夫之兄子尚女妻之。

translations.literal: The Princess of Quan, having a rift with Crown Prince He, wished to secure her own position in advance; she repeatedly praised Liang's merits and had her husband's elder brother's son Shang's daughter marry him.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Quan, having a rift with Crown Prince Sun He, wished to secure her own position in advance. She repeatedly praised Sun Liang's virtues and had her husband's elder brother's son Quan Shang's daughter marry him.

sentences.zh: 吳主以魯王霸結朋黨以害其兄，心亦惡之，謂侍中孫峻曰：「子弟不睦，臣下分部，將有袁氏之敗，為天下笑。

translations.literal: Wu's ruler, because Prince of Lu Ba had formed factions to harm his elder brother, hated this in his heart as well; he said to Palace Attendant Sun Jun: "When sons and younger brothers are not harmonious and ministers divide into factions, there will be a fall like the Yuans', and the realm will laugh.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan, seeing that Prince of Lu Sun Ba had formed factions to harm his elder brother, hated this as well. He said to Palace Attendant Sun Jun, "When sons and younger brothers are not harmonious and ministers divide into factions, there will be a fall like the Yuans', and the realm will laugh.

sentences.zh: 若使一人立者，安得不亂乎！

translations.literal: If one alone is established, how can there not be disorder!"
translations.idiomatic: If only one heir is established, how can there fail to be disorder!"

sentences.zh: 」遂有廢和立亮之意，然猶沉吟者歷年。

translations.literal: " He thereupon had the intention of deposing He and establishing Liang, yet still hesitated for years.
translations.idiomatic: " He thereupon intended to depose Sun He and establish Sun Liang, yet still hesitated for years.

sentences.zh: 峻，靜之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Jun was the great-grandson of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jun was the great-grandson of Sun Jing.

sentences.zh: 秋，吳主遂幽太子和。

translations.literal: In autumn, Wu's ruler thereupon confined Crown Prince He.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, Sun Quan confined Crown Prince Sun He.

sentences.zh: 驃騎將軍朱據諫曰：「太子，國之本根。

translations.literal: Flying Cavalry General Zhu Ju remonstrated, saying, "The crown prince is the root of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Flying Cavalry General Zhu Ju remonstrated, saying, "The crown prince is the root of the state.

sentences.zh: 加以雅性仁孝，天下歸心。

translations.literal: Moreover his refined nature is benevolent and filial; all under Heaven turn their hearts to him.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover his refined nature is benevolent and filial, and all under Heaven turn their hearts to him.

sentences.zh: 昔晉獻用驪姬而申生不存，漢武信江充而戾太子冤死，臣竊懼太子不堪其憂，雖立思子之宮，無所復及矣！

translations.literal: Formerly Duke Xian of Jin employed Li Ji and Shen Sheng did not survive; Emperor Wu of Han trusted Jiang Chong and Crown Prince Li was unjustly killed—I privately fear the crown prince will not bear his grief; though one may later build a Palace of Longing for a Son, nothing can be recovered!
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Duke Xian of Jin employed Li Ji and Crown Prince Shen Sheng did not survive. Emperor Wu of Han trusted Jiang Chong and Crown Prince Liu Ju was unjustly killed. I privately fear the crown prince will not bear his grief. Though one may later build a Palace of Longing for a Son, nothing can be undone!

sentences.zh: 」吳主不聽。

translations.literal: " Wu's ruler would not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: " Sun Quan would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 據與尚書僕射屈晃率諸將吏泥頭自縛，連日詣闕請和；

translations.literal: Ju together with Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Qu Huang led the generals and officials with mud on their heads and self-bound, for days on end coming to the palace gate to request He;
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ju together with Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Qu Huang led the generals and officials with mud on their heads and ropes upon themselves, coming day after day to the palace gate to plead for Sun He;

sentences.zh: 吳主登白爵觀，見，甚惡之，敕據、晃等「無事匆匆」。

translations.literal: Wu's ruler ascended the White Sparrow Watchtower, saw them, and greatly hated it; he charged Ju, Huang, and the rest, "Nothing is the matter—why this hurry."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan ascended the White Sparrow Watchtower, saw them, and was greatly displeased. He told Zhu Ju, Qu Huang, and the rest, "Nothing is amiss—why this commotion."

sentences.zh: 無難督陳正、五營督陳象各上書切諫，據、晃亦固諫不已；

translations.literal: Supervisor of the Wunan Chen Zheng and Supervisor of the Five Camps Chen Xiang each submitted memorials with stern remonstrance; Ju and Huang also pressed their remonstrance without cease;
translations.idiomatic: Supervisor of Wunan Chen Zheng and Supervisor of the Five Camps Chen Xiang each submitted stern memorials of remonstrance, and Zhu Ju and Qu Huang also pressed their advice without cease;

sentences.zh: 吳主大怒，族誅正、象。

translations.literal: Wu's ruler was greatly enraged and executed Zheng and Xiang together with their clans.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan was greatly enraged and executed Chen Zheng and Chen Xiang together with their entire clans.

sentences.zh: 牽據、晃入殿，據、晃猶口諫，叩頭流血，辭氣不撓。

translations.literal: He had Ju and Huang dragged into the hall; Ju and Huang still remonstrated orally, knocking their heads until blood flowed, their words and spirit unyielding.
translations.idiomatic: He had Zhu Ju and Qu Huang dragged into the hall. They still remonstrated aloud, knocking their heads until blood flowed, their words and bearing unyielding.

sentences.zh: 吳主杖之各一百，左遷據為新都郡丞，晃斥歸田裡，群司坐諫誅放者以十數。

translations.literal: Wu's ruler beat them each a hundred blows; Ju was demoted to Assistant Administrator of Xindu commandery, Huang was expelled to return to his fields; officials implicated in remonstrance who were executed or banished numbered more than ten.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan had them beaten, a hundred blows each. Zhu Ju was demoted to Assistant Administrator of Xindu commandery, Qu Huang was expelled to return to his fields, and more than ten officials implicated in the remonstrance were executed or banished.

sentences.zh: 遂廢太子和為庶人，徙故鄣，賜魯王霸死。

translations.literal: He thereupon deposed Crown Prince He as a commoner and moved him to Gucang; he granted Prince of Lu Ba death.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon deposed Crown Prince Sun He to commoner status and moved him to Gucang, and ordered Prince of Lu Sun Ba to commit suicide.

sentences.zh: 殺楊竺，流其屍於江，又誅全寄、吳安、孫奇，皆以其黨霸譖和故也。

translations.literal: He killed Yang Zhu, floated his corpse down the river, and also executed Quan Ji, Wu An, and Sun Qi—all because as partisans of Ba they had slandered He.
translations.idiomatic: He killed Yang Zhu and cast his corpse into the river, and also executed Quan Ji, Wu An, and Sun Qi—all because as partisans of Sun Ba they had slandered Sun He.

sentences.zh: 初，楊竺少獲聲名，而陸遜謂之終敗，勸竺兄穆令與之別族。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yang Zhu had early won renown, but Lu Xun said he would end in ruin and urged Zhu's elder brother Mu to have their clans separate.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yang Zhu had won renown in his youth, but Lu Xun said he would end in ruin and urged his elder brother Yang Mu to break off the clan relationship.

sentences.zh: 及竺敗，穆以數諫戒竺得免死。

translations.literal: When Zhu fell, Mu, because he had repeatedly admonished and warned Zhu, was spared death.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Zhu fell, Yang Mu was spared death because he had repeatedly admonished and warned him.

sentences.zh: 朱據未至官，中書令孫弘以詔書追賜死。

translations.literal: Before Zhu Ju reached his post, Palace Secretary Sun Hong pursued him with an imperial command ordering him to commit suicide.
translations.idiomatic: Before Zhu Ju reached his new post, Palace Secretary Sun Hong sent an imperial command ordering him to commit suicide.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，廬江太守譙郡文欽偽叛，以誘吳偏將軍朱異，欲使異自將兵迎己。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month: Lujiang Administrator Wen Qin of Qiao commandery feigned rebellion to lure Wu's Major General Zhu Yi, wishing to have Yi personally lead troops to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, Lujiang Administrator Wen Qin of Qiao commandery feigned rebellion to lure Wu's Major General Zhu Yi, hoping Yi would personally lead troops to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 異知其詐，表吳主，以為欽不可迎。

translations.literal: Yi knew it was deceit and memorialized Wu's ruler, saying Qin should not be welcomed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yi saw through the ruse and memorialized Sun Quan, saying Wen Qin should not be welcomed.

sentences.zh: 吳主曰：「方今北土未一，欽欲歸命，宜且遼之。

translations.literal: Wu's ruler said: "Now the northern lands are not yet united; Qin wishes to submit—he should for the moment be treated with distant courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan said, "Now the northern lands are not yet united. Wen Qin wishes to submit—we should for the moment receive him with due courtesy.

sentences.zh: 若嫌其有譎者，但當設計網以羅之，盛重兵以防之耳。

translations.literal: If one suspects treachery in him, one need only set schemes and nets to entrap him and concentrate heavy troops to guard against him—that is all."
translations.idiomatic: If you suspect treachery, you need only lay snares to catch him and concentrate heavy forces to guard against him—that is all."

sentences.zh: 」乃遣偏將軍呂據督二萬人，與異並力至北界，欽果不降。

translations.literal: " He then sent Major General Lü Ju supervising twenty thousand men to join with Yi in force to the northern border; Qin indeed did not surrender.
translations.idiomatic: " He then sent Major General Lü Ju at the head of twenty thousand men to join Zhu Yi and march to the northern border. Wen Qin indeed did not surrender.

sentences.zh: 異，桓之子；

translations.literal: Yi was Huan's son;
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yi was the son of Zhu Huan;

sentences.zh: 據，范之子也。

translations.literal: Ju was Fan's son.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Ju was the son of Lü Fan.

sentences.zh: 十一月，大利景侯孫禮卒。

translations.literal: Eleventh month: Sun Li, Marquis of Dalijing, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Sun Li, Marquis of Dalijing, died.

sentences.zh: 吳主立子亮為太子。

translations.literal: Wu's ruler established his son Liang as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan established his son Sun Liang as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 吳主遣軍十萬作堂邑塗塘以淹北道。

translations.literal: Wu's ruler sent an army of a hundred thousand to build the Tangtang dyke at Tangyi to flood the northern road.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan sent an army of a hundred thousand to build the Tangyi dyke at Tangyi to flood the northern approach.

sentences.zh: 十二月，甲辰，東海定王霖卒。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, day Jiachen: Prince Ding of Donghai, Lin, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the day jiachen, Prince Ding of Donghai, Cao Lin, died.

sentences.zh: 征南將軍王昶上言：「孫權流放良臣，適庶分爭，可乘釁擊吳。

translations.literal: Campaign-in-Chief of the South Wang Chang submitted a memorial: "Sun Quan has banished worthy ministers; legitimate and secondary sons contend—Wu may be struck by taking advantage of the rift."
translations.idiomatic: Campaign-in-Chief of the South Wang Chang submitted a memorial: "Sun Quan has banished worthy ministers, and legitimate and secondary sons are at odds. We may seize this opening to strike Wu."

sentences.zh: 」朝廷從之，遣新城太守南陽州泰襲巫、秭歸，荊州刺史王基向夷陵，昶向江陵。

translations.literal: " The court followed this, sending Xincheng Administrator Zhou Tai of Nanyang to raid Wu and Zigui, Jing Province Inspector Wang Ji toward Yiling, and Chang toward Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: " The court agreed, sending Xincheng Administrator Zhou Tai of Nanyang to raid Wu and Zigui, Jing Province Inspector Wang Ji toward Yiling, and Wang Chang toward Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 昶引竹絲亙為橋，渡水擊之，吳大將施績，夜遁入江陵。

translations.literal: Chang drew bamboo filaments across as a bridge, crossed the water and struck them; Wu's Grand General Shi Ji fled by night into Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chang laid bamboo filaments across the water as a bridge, crossed and attacked. Wu's Grand General Shi Ji fled by night into Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 昶欲引致平地與戰，乃先遣五軍案大道發還，使吳望見而喜；

translations.literal: Chang wished to draw them to level ground to fight; he first sent five armies to withdraw along the great road in order, so that Wu would see and rejoice;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chang wished to draw the enemy to level ground and give battle. He first sent five armies to withdraw in order along the main road, so the Wu forces would see and rejoice;

sentences.zh: 又以所獲鎧馬甲首環城以怒之，設伏兵以待之。

translations.literal: and also displayed captured armor, horses, and heads in a ring around the city to anger them, setting ambush troops to await them.
translations.idiomatic: and also displayed captured armor, horses, and heads in a ring around the city to provoke them, setting ambush troops in wait.

sentences.zh: 績果來追，昶與戰，大破之，斬其將鐘離茂、許旻。

translations.literal: Ji did indeed come in pursuit; Chang fought him and inflicted a great defeat, beheading his generals Zhongli Mao and Xu Min.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Ji did come in pursuit. Wang Chang gave battle and inflicted a great defeat, beheading his generals Zhongli Mao and Xu Min.

sentences.zh: 漢姜維復寇西平，不克。

translations.literal: Jiang Wei of Han again raided Xiping but did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei of Han again raided Xiping but failed to take it.

sentences.zh: 邵陵厲公中嘉平三年（

translations.literal: Deposed Emperor of Shaoling, Jiaping year three (
translations.idiomatic: Deposed Emperor of Shaoling, Jiaping year 3 (

sentences.zh: 辛未，公元二五一年）

translations.literal: Xinwei, the year 251 of the Common Era)
translations.idiomatic: xinwei cycle, AD 251)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，王基、州泰擊吳兵，皆破之，降者數千口。

translations.literal: Spring, first month: Wang Ji and Zhou Tai struck Wu troops and both defeated them; those who surrendered numbered several thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Wang Ji and Zhou Tai attacked Wu forces and both defeated them. Several thousand persons surrendered.

sentences.zh: 三月，以尚書令司馬孚為司空。

translations.literal: Third month: Director of the Masters of Writing Sima Fu was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Director of the Masters of Writing Sima Fu was made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，甲申，以王昶為征南大將軍。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day Jiashen: Wang Chang was made Grand General Campaigning-in-Chief of the South.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on the day jiashen, Wang Chang was made Grand General Campaigning-in-Chief of the South.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，大赦。

translations.literal: Day Renchen: a great amnesty was declared.
translations.idiomatic: On the day renchen, a great amnesty was declared.

sentences.zh: 太尉王凌聞吳人塞塗水，欲因此發兵，大嚴諸軍，表求討賊：詔報不聽。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Wang Ling, hearing that Wu men had blocked the Tushui, wished to raise troops on this pretext; he greatly marshaled the armies and submitted a memorial requesting to campaign against the enemy—the imperial response was refusal.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Wang Ling, hearing that Wu forces had dammed the Tushui, wished to use this as a pretext to mobilize. He greatly marshaled the armies and submitted a memorial requesting permission to campaign against the enemy. The imperial response was refusal.

sentences.zh: 凌遣將軍楊弘以廢立事告兗州刺史黃華，華、弘連名以白司馬懿，懿將中軍乘水道討凌，先下赦赦凌罪，又為書諭凌，已而大軍掩至百尺。

translations.literal: Ling sent General Yang Hong to inform Yanzhou Inspector Huang Hua of the plan to depose and establish; Hua and Hong jointly signed a report to Sima Yi; Yi led the central army by water route to campaign against Ling, first issuing an edict pardoning Ling's crime, also writing a letter to instruct Ling—then before long the great army suddenly arrived at Baichi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ling sent General Yang Hong to inform Yanzhou Inspector Huang Hua of the plot to depose and establish a new emperor. Huang Hua and Yang Hong jointly reported this to Sima Yi. Sima Yi led the central army by water to suppress Wang Ling, first issuing an edict pardoning his crimes and also writing to instruct him—then before long the main army suddenly appeared at Baichi.

sentences.zh: 凌自知勢窮，乃乘船單出迎懿，遣掾王彧謝罪，送印綬、節鉞。

translations.literal: Ling knew his situation was desperate; he then took a boat alone to meet Yi, sending clerk Wang Yu to apologize and surrendering his seal cord and credentials of authority.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ling knew his position was hopeless. He took a boat alone to meet Sima Yi, sending clerk Wang Yu to apologize and surrendering his seal and credentials of authority.

sentences.zh: 懿軍到丘頭，凌面縛水次，懿承詔遣主簿解其縛。

translations.literal: When Yi's army reached Qiutou, Ling bound his own face at the water's edge; Yi, acting on the imperial command, sent his registrar to unbind him.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Yi's army reached Qiutou, Wang Ling bound himself at the water's edge. Sima Yi, acting on the imperial command, sent his registrar to unbind him.

sentences.zh: 凌既蒙赦，加恃舊好，不復自疑，逕乘小船欲趨懿。

translations.literal: Ling, having received pardon, moreover relying on old friendship, no longer doubted himself; he straightway took a small boat wishing to hurry to Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Having received pardon and trusting in their old friendship, Wang Ling no longer suspected treachery. He straightway took a small boat intending to go straight to Sima Yi.

sentences.zh: 懿使人逆止之，住船淮中，相去十餘丈。

translations.literal: Yi sent a man to meet and stop him; the boat stopped mid-Huai, the two separated by more than ten zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi sent a man to stop him. The boat halted midstream on the Huai, the two men more than ten zhang apart.

sentences.zh: 凌知見外，乃遙謂懿曰：「卿直以折簡召我，我當敢不至邪，而乃引軍來乎！

translations.literal: Ling knew he was treated as an outsider; he then called to Yi from afar: "You needed only send a folded letter to summon me—would I have dared not come? Yet you lead an army instead!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ling knew he was being shut out. He called across to Sima Yi, "You needed only send a folded note summoning me—would I have dared refuse? Yet you bring an army instead!"

sentences.zh: 」懿曰：「以卿非肯逐折簡者故也。

translations.literal: " Yi said: "Because you are not one who would obey a folded letter."
translations.idiomatic: " Sima Yi said, "Because you are not one who would obey a folded note."

sentences.zh: 」凌曰：「卿負我！

translations.literal: " Ling said: "You have wronged me!"
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Ling said, "You have betrayed me!"

sentences.zh: 」懿曰：「我寧負卿，不負國家！

translations.literal: " Yi said: "I would rather wrong you than wrong the state!"
translations.idiomatic: " Sima Yi said, "I would rather wrong you than wrong the state!"

sentences.zh: 」遂遣步騎六百送凌西詣京師，凌試索棺釘以觀懿意，懿命給之。

translations.literal: " He then sent six hundred infantry and cavalry to escort Ling west to the capital; Ling tried asking for coffin nails to observe Yi's intent, and Yi ordered them given to him.
translations.idiomatic: " He then sent six hundred infantry and cavalry to escort Wang Ling west to the capital. Wang Ling tested Sima Yi's intentions by asking for coffin nails, and Sima Yi ordered them provided.

sentences.zh: 五月，甲寅，凌行到項，遂飲藥死。

translations.literal: Fifth month, day Jiayin: Ling, traveling, reached Xiang and thereupon drank poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the day jiayin, Wang Ling reached Xiang on the road and thereupon drank poison and died.

sentences.zh: 懿進至壽春，張式等皆自首。

translations.literal: Yi advanced to Shouchun; Zhang Shi and the rest all surrendered themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi advanced to Shouchun. Zhang Shi and the others all surrendered themselves.

sentences.zh: 懿窮治其事，諸相連者悉夷三族。

translations.literal: Yi thoroughly investigated the affair; all those connected were exterminated to the third degree of kinship.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi thoroughly investigated the affair. All those implicated were exterminated to the third degree of kinship.

sentences.zh: 發凌、愚塚，剖棺暴屍於所近市三日，燒其印綬、朝服，親土埋之。

translations.literal: He opened the tombs of Ling and Yu, cut open the coffins and exposed the corpses in the nearest market for three days, burned their seal cords and court robes, and buried them in person with earth.
translations.idiomatic: He opened the tombs of Wang Ling and Linghu Yu, cut open the coffins and exposed the corpses in the nearest market for three days, burned their seal cords and court robes, and buried them himself with his own hands.

sentences.zh: 初，令狐愚為白衣時，常有高志，眾人謂愚必興令狐氏。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Linghu Yu was still a commoner, he often had lofty ambitions; the multitude said Yu would surely bring glory to the Linghu clan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Linghu Yu was still a commoner, he often harbored lofty ambitions. People said he would surely bring glory to the Linghu clan.

sentences.zh: 族父弘農太守邵獨以為：「愚性倜儻，不修德而願大，必滅我宗。

translations.literal: His clansman-by-marriage Hongnong Administrator Shao alone held: "Yu's nature is free and unrestrained; he cultivates no virtue yet hopes for greatness—he will surely destroy our clan."
translations.idiomatic: His clansman-by-marriage Hongnong Administrator Shao alone held, "Yu is free-spirited and ungoverned. He cultivates no virtue yet aims high—he will surely destroy our clan."

sentences.zh: 」愚聞之，心甚不平。

translations.literal: " Yu heard this and was greatly displeased in heart.
translations.idiomatic: " Linghu Yu heard this and was deeply offended.

sentences.zh: 及邵為虎賁中郎將，而愚仕進已多所更歷，所在有名稱。

translations.literal: When Shao became Tiger-Fang Commandant and Yu in his official advancement had already passed through many posts, wherever he went he had reputation.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Shao became Captain of the Tiger Guard and Linghu Yu had risen through many posts, wherever Yu served he won renown.

sentences.zh: 愚從容謂邵曰：「先時聞大人謂愚為不繼，今竟雲何邪？

translations.literal: Yu calmly said to Shao: "Earlier I heard the elder say I would not carry on the family—what of it now?"
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Yu said calmly to Shao, "Earlier I heard you say I would not carry on the family name. What do you say now?"

sentences.zh: 」邵熟視而不答，私謂妻子曰：「公治性度，猶如故也。

translations.literal: Shao stared at him intently and did not answer; privately he told his wife and children: "His temperament and conduct in governance are still as before.
translations.idiomatic: Shao stared at him intently and made no reply. Privately he told his wife and children, "His temperament and conduct in office are still as before.

sentences.zh: 以吾觀之，終當敗滅，但不知我久當坐之不邪，將逮汝曹耳。

translations.literal: In my judgment, he will eventually meet ruin and destruction—only I do not know whether I myself will long have to sit and wait for it, or whether it will reach you all instead.
translations.idiomatic: As I see it, he will eventually meet ruin—but I do not know whether I myself will have long to wait, or whether it will reach you instead.

sentences.zh: 」邵沒後十餘年而愚族滅。

translations.literal: " More than ten years after Shao's death, Yu's clan was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten years after Shao died, the Linghu clan was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 愚在兗州，辟山陽單固為別駕，與治中楊康並為愚腹心。

translations.literal: When Yu was in Yanzhou, he recruited Shan Gu of Shanyang as Attendant Officer; he and Director Yang Kang were together Yu's inner confidants.
translations.idiomatic: While Yu served in Yanzhou, he recruited Shan Gu of Shanyang as Attendant Officer. He and Director Yang Kang were both Yu's closest confidants.

sentences.zh: 及愚卒，康應司徒辟，至洛陽，露愚陰事，愚由是敗。

translations.literal: When Yu died, Kang answered a summons from the Excellency over the Masses, went to Luoyang, and exposed Yu's secret affairs—Yu was thereby ruined.
translations.idiomatic: After Yu died, Yang Kang answered a summons from the Excellency over the Masses and went to Luoyang, where he exposed Yu's secret designs. Yu's conspiracy was thereby uncovered.

sentences.zh: 懿至壽春，見單固，問曰：「令狐反乎？

translations.literal: Yi reached Shouchun, saw Shan Gu, and asked: "Did Linghu rebel?
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Yi reached Shouchun, he saw Shan Gu and asked, "Did Linghu Yu rebel?

sentences.zh: 」曰：「無有。

translations.literal: " He replied: "There was nothing of the sort.
translations.idiomatic: " Gu replied, "Nothing of the sort.

sentences.zh: 」楊康白事，事與固連，遂收捕固及家屬皆系廷尉，考實數十，固固雲無有。

translations.literal: " Yang Kang reported the matter; the affair connected with Gu, so Gu and his family were all arrested and imprisoned in the Court of Justice; interrogated scores of times, Gu stubbornly maintained there was nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Kang then reported the affair. Since it implicated Gu, Gu and his entire family were arrested and held at the Court of Justice. Though interrogated dozens of times, Gu stubbornly denied everything.

sentences.zh: 懿錄楊康，與固對相詰，固辭窮，乃罵康曰：「老傭！

translations.literal: Yi took Yang Kang into custody and had him confront and question Gu face to face; Gu's arguments exhausted, whereupon he cursed Kang: "Old hireling!
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi brought Yang Kang in and had him confront Gu. When Gu could no longer defend himself, he cursed Kang: "Old hireling!

sentences.zh: 既負使君，又滅我族，顧汝當活邪！

translations.literal: Having betrayed our lord and destroyed my clan as well—do you think you will live!
translations.idiomatic: You betrayed our lord and destroyed my clan as well—do you think you will live!

sentences.zh: 」康初自冀封侯，後以辭頗參錯，亦並斬之。

translations.literal: " Kang had at first hoped to be enfeoffed as marquis, but afterward because his testimony was rather inconsistent, he too was beheaded along with the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Kang had at first hoped to be enfeoffed as marquis, but because his testimony was inconsistent, he too was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 臨刑，俱出獄，固又罵康曰：「老奴！

translations.literal: Facing execution, they were both led out of prison; Gu again cursed Kang: "Old slave!
translations.idiomatic: On the day of execution, as they were led out of prison together, Gu cursed Kang again: "Old slave!

sentences.zh: 汝死自分耳。

translations.literal: Your death is no more than what you deserve.
translations.idiomatic: Your death is no more than you deserve.

sentences.zh: 若令死者有知，汝何面目以行地下乎！

translations.literal: If the dead have consciousness, with what face will you walk in the underworld!
translations.idiomatic: If the dead have consciousness, with what face will you walk the underworld!

sentences.zh: 詔以揚州刺史諸葛誕為鎮東將軍，都督揚州諸軍事。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Yangzhou Inspector Zhuge Dan as General Who Pacifies the East, commanding all military affairs of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Yangzhou Inspector Zhuge Dan General Who Pacifies the East, with overall command of Yangzhou military affairs.

sentences.zh: 吳主立潘夫人為皇后，大赦，改元太元。

translations.literal: Wu's ruler established Lady Pan as empress, declared a great amnesty, and changed the era name to Taixuan.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan established Lady Pan as empress, declared a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Taixuan.

sentences.zh: 六月，賜楚王彪死。

translations.literal: Sixth month: Prince of Chu Biao was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Prince of Chu Cao Biao was ordered to commit suicide.

sentences.zh: 盡錄諸王公置鄴，使有司察之，不得與人交關。

translations.literal: All princes and dukes were summarily recorded and placed at Ye; officials were charged to watch them, and they were not permitted to associate with others.
translations.idiomatic: All imperial princes were registered and confined at Ye. Officials were charged to keep watch on them, and they were forbidden to associate with outsiders.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，壬戌，皇后甄氏殂。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, day Renxu: Empress Zhen died.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day renxu, Empress Zhen died.

sentences.zh: 辛未，以司馬孚為太尉。

translations.literal: Day Xinwei: Sima Fu was made Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinwei, Sima Fu was appointed Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 八月，戊寅，舞陽宣文侯司馬懿卒。

translations.literal: Eighth month, day Wuyin: Sima Yi, Marquis of Xuanwen of Wuyang, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the day wuyin, Sima Yi, Marquis of Xuanwen of Wuyang, died.

sentences.zh: 詔以其子衛將軍師為撫軍大將軍，錄尚書事。

translations.literal: An edict made his son Shi, General of the Guard, Grand General Who Pacifies the Army and Recorder of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed his son Sima Shi, General of the Guard, Grand General Who Pacifies the Army, with authority to record affairs for the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 初，南匈奴自謂其先本漢室之甥，因冒姓劉氏。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Southern Xiongnu claimed that their ancestors were originally nephews of the Han house and therefore assumed the surname Liu.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Southern Xiongnu claimed that their ancestors were originally nephews of the Han house and therefore took the surname Liu.

sentences.zh: 太祖留單于呼廚泉之鄴，分其眾為五部，居并州境內。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor kept the Chanyu Huchuquan at Ye, divided their people into five divisions, and settled them within Bingzhou territory.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao had kept Chanyu Huchuquan at Ye, divided the Xiongnu into five divisions, and settled them within Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 左賢王豹，單于於扶羅之子也，為左部帥，部族最強。

translations.literal: Left Worthy King Bao, son of Chanyu Yufuluo, was commander of the left division; his tribe was the strongest.
translations.idiomatic: Left Worthy King Liu Bao, son of Chanyu Yufuluo, commanded the left division—his tribe was the strongest.

sentences.zh: 城陽太守鄧艾上言：「單于在內，羌夷失統，合散無主。

translations.literal: Chengyang Administrator Deng Ai submitted a memorial: "With the Chanyu kept within the interior, the Qiang and barbarians have lost their leadership; gathered and scattered, they have no master.
translations.idiomatic: Chengyang Administrator Deng Ai submitted a memorial: "With the Chanyu kept in the interior, the Qiang and other tribes have lost unified leadership—they gather and scatter with no master.

sentences.zh: 今單于之尊日疏而外土之威日重，則胡虜不可不深備也。

translations.literal: Now the Chanyu's authority grows daily more remote while the power of the outer tribes grows daily more weighty—therefore the northern barbarians cannot but be deeply guarded against.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Chanyu's authority grows ever more remote while power on the frontier grows ever heavier—the northern tribes cannot but be guarded against with utmost vigilance.

sentences.zh: 聞劉豹部有叛胡，可因叛割為二國，以分其勢。

translations.literal: I hear that in Liu Bao's division there are rebellious Hu; one may take advantage of the rebellion to divide them into two states and thereby split their strength.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that Liu Bao's division includes rebellious tribes. We could use this rebellion to divide them into two groups and thereby split their power.

sentences.zh: 去卑功顯前朝而子不繼業，宜加其子顯號，使居雁門。

translations.literal: Qubili's achievements were manifest in the former dynasty, yet his son did not succeed to his enterprise—his son should be granted a distinguished title and settled at Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: Qubili's achievements were notable in the former dynasty, yet his son did not inherit his position. His son should be granted a distinguished title and settled at Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 離國弱寇，追錄舊勳，此御邊長計也。

translations.literal: Separating states to weaken the enemy and recording old merit—this is the long-term plan for guarding the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Dividing them to weaken the enemy and honoring past service—this is the long-term strategy for controlling the frontier.

sentences.zh: 」又陳「羌胡與民同處者，宜以漸出之，使居民表，以崇廉恥之教，塞奸宄之路。

translations.literal: " He also submitted: "Where Qiang and Hu live together with the common people, they should gradually be moved out so that residents register on household rolls, thereby promoting the teaching of integrity and shame and blocking the road of treachery and crime.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed that where Qiang and Hu lived among Chinese subjects, they should gradually be relocated so that residents could be properly registered—thereby promoting moral discipline and blocking the path of crime.

sentences.zh: 」司馬師皆從之。

translations.literal: " Sima Shi followed all of it.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shi adopted all these recommendations.

sentences.zh: 吳立節中郎將陸抗屯柴桑，詣建業治病。

translations.literal: Wu appointed Central Army Commandant Lu Kang to garrison Chaisang; he went to Jianye to seek medical treatment.
translations.idiomatic: Wu had Army Commandant Lu Kang garrison Chaisang. He went to Jianye to seek medical treatment.

sentences.zh: 病差，當還，吳主涕泣與別，謂曰：「吾前聽用讒言，與汝父大義不篤，以此負汝；

translations.literal: When his illness improved and he was about to return, Wu's ruler wept in parting and said to him: "Earlier I listened to slanderous words and was not steadfast in great righteousness toward your father—I wrong you thereby;
translations.idiomatic: When his illness improved and he was about to return, Sun Quan wept as they parted and said, "Earlier I listened to slander and failed your father in fundamental duty—I wronged you thereby;

sentences.zh: 前後所問，一焚滅之，莫令人見也。

translations.literal: whatever I asked you before and after—burn all of it; let no one see it.
translations.idiomatic: burn everything I ever asked you about, before and after—let no one see it.

sentences.zh: 是時，吳主頗寤太子和之無罪，冬，十一月，吳主祀南郊還，得風疾，欲召和還；

translations.literal: At this time Wu's ruler had come rather to realize Crown Prince He's innocence. Winter, eleventh month: returning from sacrificing at the southern suburb, he contracted a wind ailment and wished to recall He;
translations.idiomatic: By this time Sun Quan had come to realize that Crown Prince Sun He was innocent. In winter, the eleventh month, returning from the southern suburb sacrifice, he contracted a palsy and wished to recall Sun He;

sentences.zh: 全公主及侍中孫峻、中書令孫弘固爭之，乃止。

translations.literal: Princess Quan and Palace Attendant Sun Jun and Director of the Secretariat Sun Hong firmly opposed it, and he thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Quan, Palace Attendant Sun Jun, and Director of the Secretariat Sun Hong strongly opposed it, and he abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 吳主以太子亮幼少，議所付託，孫峻薦大將軍諸葛恪可付大事。

translations.literal: Wu's ruler, because Crown Prince Liang was young, deliberated on whom to entrust affairs; Sun Jun recommended Grand General Zhuge Ke as one to whom great matters could be entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: Because Crown Prince Sun Liang was still young, Sun Quan deliberated on whom to entrust the realm. Sun Jun recommended Grand General Zhuge Ke as the man to whom great affairs could be entrusted.

sentences.zh: 吳主嫌恪剛很自用，峻曰：「當今朝臣之才，無及恪者。

translations.literal: Wu's ruler disliked Ke's harsh obstinacy and self-will; Jun said: "Among the court ministers of today, none matches Ke in talent.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan disliked Ke's harsh stubbornness and self-will. Sun Jun said, "Among today's court ministers, none match Zhuge Ke in talent.

sentences.zh: 」乃召恪於武昌。

translations.literal: " He then summoned Ke from Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: He then summoned Zhuge Ke from Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 恪將行，上大將軍呂岱戒之曰：「世方多難，子每事必十思。

translations.literal: As Ke was about to depart, Superior Grand General Lü Dai admonished him: "The age is beset with many difficulties—you must reflect ten times on every matter.
translations.idiomatic: As Zhuge Ke was about to depart, Superior Grand General Lü Dai admonished him: "These are times of great difficulty—you must think ten times about every matter.

sentences.zh: 」恪曰：「昔季文子三思而後行，夫子曰：『再思可矣。

translations.literal: " Ke said: "In old times Ji Wenzi reflected thrice before acting; the Master said: 'Twice is enough.
translations.idiomatic: Ke replied, "In ancient times Ji Wenzi reflected thrice before acting, and Confucius said, 'Twice is enough.

sentences.zh: 』今君令恪十思，明恪之劣也！

translations.literal: '" Now my lord orders Ke to reflect ten times—this clearly shows Ke's inferiority!
translations.idiomatic: Now you order me to think ten times—you clearly consider me inferior!

sentences.zh: 」岱無以答，時鹹謂之失言。

translations.literal: " Dai had nothing to reply; people of the time all considered this a misstep in speech.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Dai had no reply. People of the time considered this a reckless remark.

sentences.zh: 虞喜論曰：夫托以天下，至重也；

translations.literal: Yu Xi commented: To entrust one with the realm is supremely weighty;
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xi commented: To entrust someone with the realm is supremely weighty;

sentences.zh: 以人臣行主威，至難也。

translations.literal: for a subject to wield the sovereign's authority is supremely difficult.
translations.idiomatic: for a subject to wield sovereign authority is supremely difficult.

sentences.zh: 兼二至而管萬機，能勝之者鮮矣。

translations.literal: To combine both supreme burdens and administer the myriad affairs of state—few can succeed at it.
translations.idiomatic: To bear both burdens and manage the myriad affairs of state—few can succeed.

sentences.zh: 呂侯，國之元耆，志度經遠，甫以十思戒之，而便以示劣見拒；

translations.literal: Marquis Lü was the state's foremost elder; his aspirations and foresight were far-reaching—he had just admonished him with "reflect ten times," yet Ke immediately showed him contempt and rejected the advice;
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Lü was a senior statesman of the realm, far-sighted in counsel. He had just admonished Ke to think ten times, yet Ke immediately treated the advice as proof of his own inferiority and rejected it;

sentences.zh: 此元遜之疏，機神不俱者也！

translations.literal: this was Yuanxun's obtuseness—spirit and readiness not present together!
translations.idiomatic: this was Yuanxun's obtuseness—judgment and alertness were not joined in one man!

sentences.zh: 若因十思之義，廣咨當世之務，聞善速於雷動，從諫急於風移，豈得殞首殿堂，死於凶豎之刃！

translations.literal: If he had taken the meaning of "ten reflections" to consult broadly on the affairs of the age, heard good counsel as swiftly as thunder strikes, and followed remonstrance as urgently as wind shifts—how could he have perished in the throne hall, dying by the blades of vile petty men!
translations.idiomatic: Had he taken the spirit of that advice to consult broadly on affairs of state, embrace good counsel as swiftly as thunder, and follow remonstrance as urgently as wind shifts—how could he have perished in the palace, cut down by base assassins!

sentences.zh: 世人奇其英辯，造次可觀，而哂呂侯無對為陋，不思安危終始之慮，是樂春藻之繁華，而忘秋實之甘口也。

translations.literal: People of the age marveled at his brilliant eloquence, admirable even in casual moments, and mocked Marquis Lü's lack of reply as vulgar—giving no thought to considerations of safety and danger from beginning to end; this is to delight in the luxuriant foliage of spring while forgetting the sweet taste of autumn fruit.
translations.idiomatic: People marveled at his brilliant repartee, striking even offhand, and mocked Marquis Lü's silence as dullness—never weighing safety from start to finish. They delighted in spring's lush display and forgot autumn's ripe fruit.

sentences.zh: 昔魏人伐蜀，蜀人御之，精嚴垂發，而費禕方與來敏對棋，意無厭倦。

translations.literal: Formerly when Wei attacked Shu, Shu men defended; preparations were precise and strict, on the verge of engagement—yet Fei Yi was just playing weiqi with Lai Min, his mind showing no weariness.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei once attacked Shu, the Shu defenses were taut and on the brink of battle—yet Fei Yi was playing weiqi with Lai Min, showing not the slightest fatigue.

sentences.zh: 敏以為必能辦賊，言其明略內定，貌無憂色也。

translations.literal: Min thought he would surely be able to handle the enemy; he said Yi's clarity of strategy was settled within, his bearing showing no sign of worry.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Min took this as proof Yi could handle the enemy—his strategy settled within, his face betraying no worry.

sentences.zh: 況長寧以為君子臨事而懼，好謀而成，蜀為蕞爾之國，而方向大敵，所規所圖，唯守與戰，何可矜己有餘，晏然無戚！

translations.literal: Moreover Changning held that the noble man, facing affairs, is apprehensive; he loves planning and then succeeds. Shu is a tiny state facing a great enemy; all it plots and designs is defense and battle—how could one pride oneself on having surplus capacity and be tranquil without concern!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Changning held that the noble man, when facing affairs, is apprehensive and achieves success through careful planning. Shu was a tiny state facing a great enemy—its only options were defense and battle. How could one pride oneself on having surplus capacity and remain untroubled!

sentences.zh: 斯乃禕性之寬簡，不防細微，卒為降人郭循所害，豈非兆見於彼而禍成於此哉！

translations.literal: This was precisely the openness and laxity of Yi's nature—he did not guard against minute matters—and he ultimately was harmed by the surrendered man Guo Xun. Was this not an omen visible there and calamity fulfilled here!
translations.idiomatic: This reflected the openness and laxity of Fei Yi's character—he did not guard against small dangers—and he was ultimately killed by the surrendered officer Guo Xun. Was this not a sign seen in one place and disaster fulfilled in another!

sentences.zh: 往聞長寧之甄文偉，今睹元遜之逆呂侯，二事體同，皆足以為世鑒也。

translations.literal: Formerly I heard of Changning's rejection of Wen Wei; now I behold Yuanxun's defiance of Marquis Lü—the two cases in form are the same, both sufficient to serve as warnings for the age.
translations.idiomatic: I once heard of Changning's rejection of Wen Wei; now I see Yuanxun's defiance of Marquis Lü—the two cases are alike, and both offer a warning to the world.

sentences.zh: 恪至建業，見吳主於臥內，受詔床下，以大將軍領太子太傅，孫弘領少傅；

translations.literal: Ke reached Jianye, saw Wu's ruler in his sickbed chamber, received the edict below the couch; as Grand General he additionally served as Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince, Sun Hong served as Junior Tutor;
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Ke reached Jianye and saw Sun Quan in his sickroom. Kneeling below the couch, he received the imperial charge. As Grand General he was also appointed Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince; Sun Hong was appointed Junior Tutor;

sentences.zh: 詔有司諸事一統於恪，惟殺生大事，然後以聞。

translations.literal: The edict ordered that all affairs of the various offices be unified under Ke; only in grave matters of life and death should he then report.
translations.idiomatic: The edict placed all government affairs under Ke's authority; only matters of life and death were to be reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 為制群官百司拜揖之儀，各有品序。

translations.literal: Regulations were made for the ceremony of bowing and salutation among the various officials and hundred offices, each with its rank and order.
translations.idiomatic: He established regulations for bowing and salutation among officials, each according to rank.

sentences.zh: 又以會稽太守北海滕胤為太常。

translations.literal: Teng Yin of Beihai, Administrator of Kuaiji, was also made Chamberlain for Ceremonials.
translations.idiomatic: Teng Yin of Beihai, Administrator of Kuaiji, was also appointed Chamberlain for Ceremonials.

sentences.zh: 胤，吳主婿也。

translations.literal: Yin was Wu's ruler's son-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Teng Yin was Sun Quan's son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 十二月，以光祿勳滎陽鄭沖為司空。

translations.literal: Twelfth month: Zheng Chong of Xingyang, Superintendent of the Imperial Household, was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Zheng Chong of Xingyang, Superintendent of the Imperial Household, was appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 漢費禕還成都，望氣者云：「都邑無宰相位。

translations.literal: Fei Yi of Han returned to Chengdu; a geomancer said: "The capital has no position for a chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Yi of Shu returned to Chengdu. A geomancer said, "The capital holds no seat for a chancellor.

sentences.zh: 」乃復北屯漢壽。

translations.literal: " He thereupon again garrisoned Han Shou to the north.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore returned north to garrison at Hanshou.

sentences.zh: 是歲，漢尚書令呂乂卒，以侍中陳祗守尚書令。

translations.literal: That year, Han's Director of the Masters of Writing Lü Yi died; Palace Attendant Chen Zhi was made acting Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: That year, Shu's Director of the Masters of Writing Lü Yi died. Palace Attendant Chen Zhi was appointed acting Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 邵陵厲公中嘉平四年（

translations.literal: Deposed Emperor of Shaoling, mid Jiaping year four (
translations.idiomatic: Deposed Emperor of Shaoling, mid Jiaping year four (

sentences.zh: 壬申，公元二五二年）

translations.literal: Renshen, the year 252 of the Common Era)
translations.idiomatic: Renshen, the year 252 of the Common Era)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，癸卯，以司馬師為大將軍。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, day Guimao: Sima Shi was made Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the day guimao, Sima Shi was appointed Grand General.

sentences.zh: 吳主立故太子和為南陽王，使居長沙；

translations.literal: Wu's ruler established the former crown prince He as Prince of Nanyang and had him reside at Changsha;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan established the former crown prince Sun He as Prince of Nanyang and sent him to reside at Changsha;

sentences.zh: 仲姬子奮為齊王，居武昌；

translations.literal: Lady Zhong's son Fen was made Prince of Qi and resided at Wuchang;
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhong's son Sun Fen was made Prince of Qi and sent to reside at Wuchang;

sentences.zh: 王夫人子休為琅邪王，居虎林。

translations.literal: Lady Wang's son Xiu was made Prince of Langye and resided at Hulin.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang's son Sun Xiu was made Prince of Langye and sent to reside at Hulin.

sentences.zh: 二月。

translations.literal: Second month.
translations.idiomatic: The second month.

sentences.zh: 立皇后張氏，大赦。

translations.literal: Empress Zhang was established; a great amnesty was declared.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhang was installed, and a general amnesty was declared.

sentences.zh: 后，故涼州刺史既之孫，東莞太守緝之女也。

translations.literal: The empress was the granddaughter of former Liangzhou Inspector Ji and the daughter of Dongguan Administrator Ji.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was the granddaughter of former Liangzhou Inspector Ji and the daughter of Dongguan Administrator Ji.

sentences.zh: 召緝拜光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Ji was summoned and appointed Supervising Director of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was summoned to court and appointed Supervising Director of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 吳人改元神鳳，大赦。

translations.literal: Wu men changed the era name to Shenfeng and declared a great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Wu changed the era name to Shenfeng and declared a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 吳潘后性剛戾，吳主疾病，后使人問孫弘以呂后稱制故事。

translations.literal: Empress Pan of Wu was by nature harsh and perverse; when Wu's ruler was ill, the empress sent someone to ask Sun Hong about Empress Lü's precedent of wielding imperial power.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Pan of Wu was harsh and violent by nature. When Sun Quan fell ill, she sent someone to ask Sun Hong about Empress Lü's precedent of ruling as regent.

sentences.zh: 左右不勝其虐，伺其昏睡，縊殺之，託言中惡。

translations.literal: Those around her could not endure her cruelty; watching for her to fall asleep, they strangled her and reported it as sudden evil affliction.
translations.idiomatic: Those around her could not endure her cruelty. When she fell asleep, they strangled her and reported that she had died of sudden affliction.

sentences.zh: 後事泄，坐死者六七人。

translations.literal: Later the affair was exposed; six or seven persons were put to death for it.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair later came to light, six or seven people were executed for it.

sentences.zh: 吳主病困，召諸葛恪、孫弘、滕胤及將軍呂據、侍中孫峻入臥內，屬以後事。

translations.literal: Wu's ruler, gravely ill, summoned Zhuge Ke, Sun Hong, Teng Yin, and General Lü Ju and Palace Attendant Sun Jun into his sickroom and entrusted them with affairs after his death.
translations.idiomatic: Gravely ill, Sun Quan summoned Zhuge Ke, Sun Hong, Teng Yin, General Lü Ju, and Palace Attendant Sun Jun to his sickroom and entrusted them with affairs after his death.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，〔乙未〕，吳主殂。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day Yiwei: Wu's ruler died.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on the day yiwei, Sun Quan died.

sentences.zh: 孫弘素與諸葛恪不平，懼為恪所治，秘不發喪，欲矯詔誅恪。

translations.literal: Sun Hong had long been at odds with Zhuge Ke; fearing Ke would punish him, he secretly withheld announcement of the death and wished to forge an edict to execute Ke.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hong had long been at odds with Zhuge Ke. Fearing Ke would punish him, he kept the death secret and planned to forge an edict to have Ke executed.

sentences.zh: 孫峻以告恪，恪請弘咨事，於坐中殺之。

translations.literal: Sun Jun informed Ke; Ke invited Hong to consult on affairs and killed him at the session.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jun informed Zhuge Ke. Ke invited Sun Hong to discuss affairs and killed him on the spot.

sentences.zh: 乃發喪。

translations.literal: Only then was the mourning announced.
translations.idiomatic: Only then was the death announced.

sentences.zh: 謚吳主曰大皇帝。

translations.literal: Wu's ruler was posthumously titled Great Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan was posthumously titled Great Emperor.

sentences.zh: 〔丁酉〕，太子亮即位，大赦，改元建興。

translations.literal: Day Dingyou: Crown Prince Liang ascended the throne, declared a great amnesty, and changed the era name to Jianxing.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingyou, Crown Prince Sun Liang ascended the throne, declared a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Jianxing.

sentences.zh: 閏月，以諸葛恪為太傅，滕胤為衛將軍，呂岱為大司馬。

translations.literal: Intercalary month: Zhuge Ke was made Grand Tutor, Teng Yin General of the Guard, Lü Dai Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, Zhuge Ke was appointed Grand Tutor, Teng Yin General of the Guard, and Lü Dai Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 恪乃命罷視聽，息校官，原逋責，除關稅，崇恩澤，眾莫不悅。

translations.literal: Ke thereupon ordered abolition of surveillance and listening-in, cessation of the inspectorate of officials, remission of overdue taxes, elimination of transit duties, and enhancement of gracious benefits—the multitude none but rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Ke then abolished surveillance and eavesdropping, suspended the office of official inspectors, remitted overdue taxes, eliminated transit duties, and extended imperial grace—the people all rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 恪每出入，百姓延頸思見其狀。

translations.literal: Whenever Ke went out or entered, the common people craned their necks longing to see his bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Ke appeared in public, the people craned their necks eager to catch sight of him.

sentences.zh: 恪不欲諸王處濱江兵馬之地，乃徙齊王奮於豫章，琅邪王休於丹陽。

translations.literal: Ke did not wish the princes to occupy lands along the river with military forces; he therefore moved Prince of Qi Fen to Yuzhang and Prince of Langye Xiu to Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ke did not want the princes stationed in riverine regions with military resources. He therefore moved Prince of Qi Sun Fen to Yuzhang and Prince of Langye Sun Xiu to Danyang.

sentences.zh: 奮不肯徙，又數越法度，恪為箋以遺奮曰：「帝王之尊，與天同位，是以家天下，臣父兄；

translations.literal: Fen refused to move and repeatedly transgressed regulations; Ke wrote a formal letter to Fen saying: "The eminence of emperor and king shares position with Heaven; therefore one makes the realm a family and treats father and elder brother as subjects;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fen refused to move and repeatedly violated regulations. Ke sent him a formal letter saying, "The emperor's dignity equals Heaven itself. Therefore he makes the realm his household and treats even father and elder brother as subjects;

sentences.zh: 仇讎有善，不得不舉，親戚有惡，不得不誅，所以承天理物，先國後身，蓋聖人立制，百代不易之道也。

translations.literal: even an enemy who has merit cannot but be advanced; even a kinsman who has evil cannot but be punished—thereby upholding Heaven's principle and ordering things, putting the state before oneself. This is the system the sages established, a Way unchanged through a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: even an enemy's merit must be rewarded, and even a kinsman's wickedness must be punished—thereby upholding Heaven's order and putting the state before oneself. This is the system the sages established—the unchanging Way for all generations.

sentences.zh: 昔漢初興，多王子弟，至於太強，輒為不軌，上則幾危社稷，下則骨肉相殘，其後懲戒以為大諱。

translations.literal: Formerly when Han first rose, many princes were enfeoffed among the imperial sons and brothers; when they grew too strong they invariably acted unlawfully—above they nearly endangered the altars of soil and grain, below they slaughtered one another among flesh and blood. Later generations took warning and made this a great taboo.
translations.idiomatic: When Han first rose, many imperial sons and brothers were enfeoffed as kings. When they grew too powerful they invariably rebelled—threatening the dynasty above and slaughtering kin below. Later generations took this as a solemn warning.

sentences.zh: 自光武以來，諸王有制，惟得自娛於宮內，不得臨民，干與政事，其與交通，皆有重禁，遂以全安，各保福祚，此則前世得失之驗也。

translations.literal: From Emperor Guangwu onward the princes were regulated: they might amuse themselves only within their palaces, might not oversee the people or meddle in government affairs; all association with others was strictly forbidden—they thereby remained secure, each preserving his blessing and rank. This is the proof of gain and loss from former ages.
translations.idiomatic: From Emperor Guangwu onward, princes were strictly regulated—they might enjoy themselves within their palaces but could not govern the people or meddle in affairs of state. Contact with outsiders was forbidden under heavy penalties. Thus they remained secure and preserved their fortunes. This is the lesson of past success and failure.

sentences.zh: 大行皇帝覽古戒今，防牙遏萌，慮於千載，是以寢疾之日，分遣諸王各早就國，詔策勤渠，科禁嚴峻，其所戒敕，無所不至。

translations.literal: The late emperor, reviewing antiquity to warn the present, checked buds and stopped sprouts, planning for a thousand years—therefore on the day his illness took hold he dispatched the various princes each to his fief early; his edicts and writs were earnest and thorough, penalties and prohibitions severe; his admonitions and commands left nothing out.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor, reviewing the past to warn the present, nipped trouble in the bud and planned for the long term. On the day his illness took hold, he sent each prince early to his fief. His edicts were earnest, his prohibitions severe, and his admonitions exhaustive.

sentences.zh: 誠欲上安宗廟，下全諸王，使百世相承，無凶國害家之悔也。

translations.literal: Truly he wished above to secure the ancestral temples and below to preserve the princes, so that they might succeed one another for a hundred generations without the regret of states bringing calamity upon their houses.
translations.idiomatic: He truly wished to secure the ancestral temples above and protect the princes below, so that succession might continue for generations without the disaster of princes ruining their own houses.

sentences.zh: 大王宜上惟太伯順父之志，中念河間獻王、東海王強恭順之節，下存前世驕恣荒亂之王以為警戒。

translations.literal: Your Highness should above reflect on Taibo's compliance with his father's intent, in the middle recall the respectful obedience of Prince Xian of Hejian and Prince Qiang of Donghai, and below keep as warning the arrogant, wanton, and disorderly kings of former ages.
