translations.idiomatic: Your Highness should look up to Taibo's obedience to his father, take as models Prince Xian of Hejian and Prince Qiang of Donghai in their respectful submission, and take as warning the arrogant and disorderly princes of past ages.

sentences.zh: 而聞頃至武昌以來，多違詔敕，不拘制度，擅發諸將兵治護宮室。

translations.literal: Yet I hear that since arriving at Wuchang you have often violated edicts and commands, disregarded regulations, and on your own authority dispatched various generals and troops to build and maintain your palace.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I hear that since your arrival at Wuchang you have repeatedly violated edicts, disregarded regulations, and on your own authority dispatched generals and troops to build and maintain your palace.

sentences.zh: 又左右常從有罪過者，當以表聞，公付有司；

translations.literal: Again when those at right and left who constantly attend had faults and offenses, you ought to report them in a memorial and publicly hand them to the responsible offices;
translations.idiomatic: When attendants in your constant following commit offenses, you should report them in a memorial and hand them over to the proper offices;

sentences.zh: 而擅私殺，事不明白。

translations.literal: yet you on your own privately killed them—the matter was not clarified.
translations.idiomatic: yet you have executed them on your own authority, and the affair was never made clear.

sentences.zh: 中書楊融，親受詔敕，所當恭肅，乃云『正自不聽禁，當如我何！

translations.literal: Chief Secretariat Yang Rong personally received edicts and commands—what was required was reverence and solemnity—yet he said, 'If I simply will not obey the ban, what can he do to me!
translations.idiomatic: Palace Writer Yang Rong personally received edicts and commands—he should have been reverent and solemn—yet he said, 'If I simply will not heed the prohibition, what can he do to me!

sentences.zh: 』聞此之日，小大驚怪，莫不寒心。

translations.literal: On the day this was heard, great and small were shocked and alarmed; none failed to feel chill at heart.
translations.idiomatic: When this was heard, great and small were startled and dismayed; none did not feel cold at heart.

sentences.zh: 裡語曰：『明鑒所以照形，古事所以知今。

translations.literal: A village saying says: 'The bright mirror is what reflects form; ancient affairs are what let one know the present.
translations.idiomatic: A village saying goes: 'The bright mirror shows form; ancient affairs let one know the present.

sentences.zh: 』大王宜深以魯王為戒，改易其行，戰戰兢兢，盡禮朝廷，如此，則無求不得。

translations.literal: ' Your Highness ought deeply to take the Prince of Lu as a warning, change and alter your conduct, tremble and fear, exhaust ritual toward the court—thus then there is nothing sought that will not be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: ' Your Highness should take the Prince of Lu as a deep warning, change your conduct, tremble with fear, exhaust all propriety toward the court—if so, nothing you seek will go ungranted.

sentences.zh: 若棄忘先帝法教，懷輕慢之心，臣下寧負大王，不敢負先帝遺詔；

translations.literal: If you abandon and forget the late emperor's laws and instruction and cherish a light and disrespectful heart, we ministers would rather wrong Your Highness than dare wrong the late emperor's entrusted charge;
translations.idiomatic: If you cast aside the late emperor's laws and teachings and harbor a mind of slight contempt, your servants would rather wrong Your Highness than dare wrong the late emperor's testamentary charge;

sentences.zh: 寧為大王所怨疾，豈敢忘尊主之威而令詔敕不行於籓臣邪！

translations.literal: would rather be resented and hated by Your Highness than dare forget the honored ruler's majesty and allow edicts and commands not to be carried out upon feudatory ministers!
translations.idiomatic: rather be resented and hated by Your Highness than dare forget the awesome authority of our sovereign and let edicts and commands fail to prevail over vassal ministers!

sentences.zh: 向使魯王早納忠直之言，懷驚懼之慮，則享祚無窮，豈有滅亡之禍哉！

translations.literal: If only the Prince of Lu had early accepted loyal and straight words and harbored alarm and fear, then he would have enjoyed the throne without end—how could there have been the disaster of destruction!
translations.idiomatic: Had the Prince of Lu early taken loyal and straight words and harbored alarm and fear, he would have enjoyed blessing without end—how could there have been the calamity of extinction!

sentences.zh: 夫良藥苦口，唯病者能甘之；

translations.literal: Good medicine is bitter in the mouth—only the ill can find it sweet;
translations.idiomatic: Good medicine is bitter in the mouth—only the sick can taste it as sweet;

sentences.zh: 忠言逆耳，唯達者能受之。

translations.literal: Loyal words oppose the ear—only the comprehending can accept them.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal words grate on the ear—only the wise can receive them.

sentences.zh: 今者恪等心婁心婁，欲為大王除危殆於萌芽，廣福慶之基原，是以不自知言至，願蒙三思！

translations.literal: Now Ke and the others, anxious and fearful, wish for Your Highness to remove danger and peril at the budding and broaden the base of blessing and fortune—therefore, unaware that our words have reached the utmost, we wish to receive threefold pondering!
translations.idiomatic: Now Ke and the others, trembling with earnest fear, wish to remove peril and danger for Your Highness while it is still a sprout and broaden the foundation of fortune and blessing; therefore, not knowing that our words have gone too far, we beg that you ponder them thrice!

sentences.zh: 」王得箋，懼，遂移南昌。

translations.literal: The prince received the memorial, feared, and then moved to Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: The prince received the memorial, took alarm, and thereupon moved to Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 初，吳大帝築東興堤以遏巢湖，其後入寇淮南，敗，以內船，遂廢不復治。

translations.literal: At first, Wu's Great Emperor built the Dongxing embankment to dam Chaohu Lake; afterward they invaded Huainan, were defeated, used inward boats, and then abandoned it and did not restore it again.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Wu's Great Emperor built the Dongxing dike to block Chaohu Lake; afterward, when they invaded Huainan and were defeated, they breached it to admit boats inward, and the work was abandoned and never restored.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，太傅恪會眾於東興，更作大堤，左右結山，俠築兩城，各留千人，使將軍全端守西城，都尉留略守東城，引軍而還。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month: Grand Tutor Ke gathered the host at Dongxing, rebuilt the great embankment, joined the mountains left and right, and built two cities in between, leaving a thousand men at each; he had General Quan Duan guard the western city and Commandant Liu Lue guard the eastern city, then withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, Grand Tutor Ke assembled the host at Dongxing, rebuilt the great dike, linked the mountains on either side, and built two cities between them, leaving a thousand men at each; he sent General Quan Duan to hold the western city and Commandant Liu Lue to hold the eastern city, then led the army back.

sentences.zh: 鎮東將軍諸葛誕言於大將軍師曰：「今因吳內侵，使文舒逼江陵，仲恭向武昌，以羈吳之上流；

translations.literal: Eastern Garrison General Zhuge Dan spoke to Grand General Sima Shi, saying: 'Now, exploiting Wu's internal incursion, have Wenshu press Jiangling and Zhonggong turn toward Wuchang, to restrain Wu's upper stream;
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Garrison General Zhuge Dan said to Grand General Sima Shi: 'Now, taking advantage of Wu's inward aggression, have Wenshu press Jiangling and Zhonggong advance on Wuchang, to tie up Wu's upper Yangtze;

sentences.zh: 然後簡精卒攻其兩城，比救至，可大獲也。

translations.literal: then choose picked crack troops to attack their two cities—when rescue arrives, a great catch can be made.'
translations.idiomatic: then select crack troops to attack the two cities—by the time relief arrives, a great haul can be taken.'

sentences.zh: 」是時征南大將軍王昶、征東將軍胡遵、鎮南將軍毋丘儉等各獻征吳之計。

translations.literal: At this time Southern Campaign General Wang Chang, Eastern Campaign General Hu Zun, and Southern Garrison General Guanqiu Jian each presented plans for attacking Wu.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Southern Campaign General Wang Chang, Eastern Campaign General Hu Zun, and Southern Garrison General Guanqiu Jian each submitted plans for campaigning against Wu.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以三征計異，詔問尚書傅嘏。

translations.literal: The court, because the three expeditionary commanders' plans differed, issued an edict asking Chief of Secretaries Fu Gu.
translations.idiomatic: The court, because the three campaigners' plans differed, edicted a query to Chief of Secretaries Fu Gu.

sentences.zh: 嘏對曰：「議者或欲泛舟徑濟，橫行江表；

translations.literal: Gu answered: 'Some in the deliberations wish to float boats and cross directly, rampaging across the Jiang region;
translations.idiomatic: Gu replied: 'Some debaters wish to float boats straight across and rampage south of the Yangtze;

sentences.zh: 或欲四道並進，攻其城壘；

translations.literal: some wish four routes together to advance and attack their ramparts;
translations.idiomatic: some wish to advance on four routes together and assault their fortifications;

sentences.zh: 或欲大佃疆場，觀釁而動；

translations.literal: some wish great garrison farming on the borderlands and act on seeing a crack;
translations.idiomatic: some wish to garrison-farm widely on the frontier and move when they see an opening;

sentences.zh: 誠皆取賊之常計也。

translations.literal: Truly all are the enemy's standard reckonings.
translations.idiomatic: Truly these are all the bandits' usual stratagems.

sentences.zh: 然自治兵以來，出入三載，非掩襲之軍也。

translations.literal: Yet from marshaling troops until now, going out and returning three years—they are not a raiding army.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from the ordering of troops until now, three years have passed in and out—it is no longer a force for surprise raids.

sentences.zh: 賊之為寇，幾六十年矣，君臣相保，吉凶共患，又喪其元帥，上下憂危，設令列船津要，堅城據險，橫行之計，其殆難捷。

translations.literal: The enemy as raiders is nearly sixty years; lord and ministers mutually preserve, fortune and misfortune share peril, and moreover they have lost their commander-in-chief—above and below worry in danger. If they line ships at the fords and hold ramparts at the narrows, the plan of rampaging will be hard to succeed quickly.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits have been raiders for nearly sixty years; lord and ministers protect one another, share fortune and misfortune, and now have also lost their commander-in-chief—above and below are anxious and imperiled. Suppose they array ships at the critical fords and hold firm cities at the narrows—the plan of rampaging would be hard to succeed swiftly.

sentences.zh: 今邊壤之守，與賊相遠，賊設羅落，又特重密，間諜不行，耳目無聞。

translations.literal: Now the borderlands' guards are far from the enemy; the enemy sets net lines that are especially heavy and close—scouts cannot operate, and there is no hearing for ears and eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Now the frontier garrisons stand far from the enemy; the enemy has set picket lines that are especially dense and tight—spies cannot operate, and we hear nothing with our ears and eyes.

sentences.zh: 夫軍無耳目，校察未詳，而舉大眾以臨巨險，此為希幸徼功，先戰而後求勝，非全軍之長策也。

translations.literal: When an army lacks ears and eyes and investigation is not detailed, yet one raises a great multitude to confront a huge peril—this is hoping for lucky achievement, first fighting and afterward seeking victory—not the long strategy of preserving the whole army.
translations.idiomatic: When an army has no ears and eyes, and reconnaissance is not thorough, yet one raises a great host to face a vast peril—this is hoping for lucky merit, fighting first and seeking victory afterward; it is not the long strategy for preserving the whole army.

sentences.zh: 唯有進軍大佃，最差完牢；

translations.literal: Only advancing the army in great garrison farming is the most complete and secure;
translations.idiomatic: Only advancing the army in great garrison farming is the most secure and complete.

sentences.zh: 可詔昶、遵等擇地居險，審所錯置，及令三方一時前守。

translations.literal: You may edict Chang, Zun, and others to choose ground and dwell in narrows, examine placement carefully, and order the three directions at once to advance and hold.
translations.idiomatic: You may edict Chang, Zun, and the others to choose terrain and occupy the narrows, examine where to place forces, and order the three directions to advance and hold at once.

sentences.zh: 奪其肥壤，使還□脊土，一也；

translations.literal: Seize their fat soil and make them return to ridge-thin land—first;
translations.idiomatic: Strip them of their rich soil and make them return to cultivate barren land—this is the first;

sentences.zh: 兵出民表，寇鈔不犯，二也；

translations.literal: Troops issue beyond the people so raiding and plundering do not violate them—second;
translations.idiomatic: Troops camp beyond the people so raiders and plunderers do not violate them—this is the second;

sentences.zh: 招懷近路，降附日至，三也；

translations.literal: Summon and cherish along the near roads; surrender and attachment arrive daily—third;
translations.idiomatic: Summon and win over those along the near roads, and surrenders and adherents arrive daily—this is the third;

sentences.zh: 羅落遠設，間構不來，四也；

translations.literal: Picket lines set far off so spies and intrigues do not come—fourth;
translations.idiomatic: Picket lines are set far off so spies and intrigues do not come—this is the fourth;

sentences.zh: 賊退其守，羅落必淺，佃作易立，五也；

translations.literal: When the bandits shrink their defense, pickets must be shallow, and garrison farming is easy to establish—fifth;
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy withdraws their guard, picket lines must be shallow and garrison farming easy to establish—this is the fifth;

sentences.zh: 坐食積穀，士不運輸，六也；

translations.literal: Sitting and eating piled grain, soldiers do not transport—sixth;
translations.idiomatic: Sitting and eating accumulated grain, soldiers need not transport supplies—this is the sixth;

sentences.zh: 釁隙時聞，討襲速決，七也；

translations.literal: Cracks are heard from time to time; punitive raids are decided with speed—seventh;
translations.idiomatic: Cracks are heard from time to time, and punitive raids are decided swiftly—this is the seventh;

sentences.zh: 凡此七者，軍事之急務也。

translations.literal: In all, these seven are the urgent tasks of war.
translations.idiomatic: In all, these seven are the urgent tasks of war.

sentences.zh: 不據則賊擅便資，據之則利歸於國，不可不察也。

translations.literal: If you do not seize them, the bandits monopolize convenient resources; if you seize them, profit returns to the state—this cannot go unexamined.
translations.idiomatic: If we do not seize them, the enemy monopolizes convenient resources; if we seize them, the profit returns to the state—this cannot go unexamined.

sentences.zh: 夫屯壘相逼，形勢已交，智勇得陳，巧拙得用，策之而知得失之計，角之而知有餘不足，虜之情偽，將焉所逃！

translations.literal: When garrison ramparts press each other and the terrain is already engaged, wisdom and courage can be displayed and skill and clumsiness put to use—plan against them and know the reckoning of gain and loss; test them and know surplus and insufficiency. Where can the barbarians' truth and falsehood escape?
translations.idiomatic: When garrison ramparts press one another and the terrain is already engaged, wisdom and courage can be displayed and skill and clumsiness put to use—plan against them and know the reckoning of gain and loss; test them and know surplus and insufficiency. Where can the barbarians' truth and falsehood escape?

sentences.zh: 夫以小敵大，則役煩力竭；

translations.literal: To use the small against the large is to wear out labor and exhaust strength;
translations.idiomatic: To use the small against the large is to wear out labor and exhaust strength;

sentences.zh: 以貧敵富，則斂重財匱。

translations.literal: To use the poor against the rich is to levy heavily and drain wealth.
translations.idiomatic: To use the poor against the rich is to levy heavily and drain wealth.

sentences.zh: 故曰：『敵逸能勞之，飽能饑之』，此之謂也。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said: 'When the enemy is at ease, you can weary him; when he is full, you can starve him'—this is what that means.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore it is said: 'When the enemy is at ease, you can weary him; when he is full, you can starve him'—this is what that means.

sentences.zh: 」司馬師不從。

translations.literal: Sima Shi did not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shi did not heed him.

sentences.zh: 十一月，詔王昶等三道擊吳。

translations.literal: Eleventh month: an edict ordered Wang Chang and the others to attack Wu on three routes.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, an edict ordered Wang Chang and the others to attack Wu on three routes.

sentences.zh: 十二月，王昶攻南郡，毋丘儉向武昌，胡遵、諸葛誕率眾七萬攻東興。

translations.literal: Twelfth month: Wang Chang attacked Nan Commandery; Guanqiu Jian turned toward Wuchang; Hu Zun and Zhuge Dan led seventy thousand men to attack Dongxing.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Wang Chang attacked Nan Commandery; Guanqiu Jian turned toward Wuchang; Hu Zun and Zhuge Dan led seventy thousand men to attack Dongxing.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，吳太傅恪將兵四萬，晨夜兼行，救東興。

translations.literal: On the day jiayin, Wu Grand Tutor Ke led forty thousand troops, marching day and night together, to relieve Dongxing.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiayin, Wu Grand Tutor Ke led forty thousand troops, marching day and night together, to relieve Dongxing.

sentences.zh: 胡遵等敕諸軍作浮橋以度，陳於坻上，分兵攻兩城。

translations.literal: Hu Zun and the others ordered the armies to build a pontoon bridge to cross and formed up on the shoal, dividing troops to attack the two cities.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zun and the others ordered the armies to build a pontoon bridge to cross and formed up on the shoal, dividing troops to attack the two cities.

sentences.zh: 城在高峻，不可卒拔。

translations.literal: The cities stood high and steep—they could not be taken at once.
translations.idiomatic: The cities stood high and steep—they could not be taken at once.

sentences.zh: 諸葛恪使冠軍將軍丁奉與呂據、留贊、唐咨為前部，從山西上。

translations.literal: Zhuge Ke sent Champion General Ding Feng, together with Lü Ju, Liu Zan, and Tang Zi, as the vanguard, ascending from the west of the mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Ke sent Champion General Ding Feng, together with Lü Ju, Liu Zan, and Tang Zi, as the vanguard, ascending from the west of the mountain.

sentences.zh: 奉謂諸將曰：「今諸軍行緩，若賊據便地，則難以爭鋒，我請趨之。

translations.literal: Feng said to the generals: 'Now the armies march slowly; if the enemy seizes favorable ground, it will be hard to contend for the advantage—I ask leave to hurry ahead.
translations.idiomatic: Feng said to the generals: 'Now the armies march slowly; if the enemy seizes favorable ground, it will be hard to contend for the advantage—I ask leave to hurry ahead.

sentences.zh: 」乃辟諸軍使下道，奉自率麾下三千人徑進。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent the other armies down the lower road, while he himself led three thousand men of his command straight forward.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he sent the other armies down the lower road, while he himself led three thousand men of his command straight forward.

sentences.zh: 時北風，奉舉帆二日，即至東關，遂據徐塘。

translations.literal: There was a north wind; Feng raised sail and in two days reached Dong Pass, then occupied Xu embankment.
translations.idiomatic: There was a north wind; Feng raised sail and in two days reached Dong Pass, then occupied Xu embankment.

sentences.zh: 時天雪，寒，胡遵等方置酒高會。

translations.literal: Snow was falling and the cold was bitter; Hu Zun and the others were just holding a grand feast with wine.
translations.idiomatic: Snow was falling and the cold was bitter; Hu Zun and the others were just holding a grand feast with wine.

sentences.zh: 奉見其前部兵少，謂其下曰：「取封侯爵賞，正在今日！

translations.literal: Feng saw their forward troops were few and said to his men: 'The titles, fiefs, and rewards await us today!
translations.idiomatic: Feng saw their forward troops were few and said to his men: 'The titles, fiefs, and rewards await us today!

sentences.zh: 」乃使兵皆解鎧，去矛戟，但兜鍪刀楯，裸身緣堨。

translations.literal: He then had the soldiers all remove their armor, discard spears and halberds, keeping only helmets, swords, and shields, and climb the ramparts bare-bodied.
translations.idiomatic: He then had the soldiers all remove their armor, discard spears and halberds, keeping only helmets, swords, and shields, and climb the ramparts bare-bodied.

sentences.zh: 魏人望見，大笑之，不即嚴兵。

translations.literal: The Wei men saw them and laughed loudly, not immediately marshaling their troops.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei men saw them and laughed loudly, not immediately marshaling their troops.

sentences.zh: 吳兵得上，便鼓噪，斫破魏前屯，呂據等繼至。

translations.literal: Once the Wu soldiers gained the height, they at once raised a battle cry, hacked through the Wei forward camp, and Lü Ju and the others followed in.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Wu soldiers gained the height, they at once raised a battle cry, hacked through the Wei forward camp, and Lü Ju and the others followed in.

sentences.zh: 魏軍驚擾散走，爭渡浮橋，橋壞絕，自投於水，更相蹈藉。

translations.literal: The Wei army was startled and scattered in flight, scrambling to cross the pontoon bridge; the bridge broke apart, and men threw themselves into the water, trampling one another.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei army was startled and scattered in flight, scrambling to cross the pontoon bridge; the bridge broke apart, and men threw themselves into the water, trampling one another.

sentences.zh: 前部督韓綜、樂安太守桓嘉等皆沒，死者數萬。

translations.literal: Forward commander Han Zong, Administrator of Le'an Huan Jia, and others all perished; the dead numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Forward commander Han Zong, Administrator of Le'an Huan Jia, and others all perished; the dead numbered in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 綜故吳叛將，數為吳害，吳大帝常切齒恨之，諸葛恪命送其首以白大帝廟。

translations.literal: Zong had been a Wu defector and repeatedly harmed Wu; Wu's Great Emperor had often gnashed his teeth in hatred of him. Zhuge Ke ordered his head sent to report the victory at the Great Emperor's temple.
translations.idiomatic: Zong had been a Wu defector and repeatedly harmed Wu; Wu's Great Emperor had often gnashed his teeth in hatred of him. Zhuge Ke ordered his head sent to report the victory at the Great Emperor's temple.

sentences.zh: 獲車乘、牛馬、騾驢各以千數，資器山積，振旅而歸。

translations.literal: They captured chariots, cattle, horses, mules, and donkeys by the thousands each, and equipment and vessels piled like hills; then they rallied the host and returned.
translations.idiomatic: They captured chariots, cattle, horses, mules, and donkeys by the thousands each, and equipment and vessels piled like hills; then they rallied the host and returned.

sentences.zh: 初，漢姜維寇西平，獲中郎將郭循，漢人以為左將軍。

translations.literal: Earlier, Han's Jiang Wei raided Xiping and captured Commandant Guo Xun; the Han court made him Left General.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Han's Jiang Wei raided Xiping and captured Commandant Guo Xun; the Han court made him Left General.

sentences.zh: 循欲刺漢主，不得親近，每因上壽，且拜且前，為左右所遏，事輒不果。

translations.literal: Xun wished to assassinate the Han ruler but could not approach him; each time at birthday felicitations he would bow and advance step by step, but was blocked by those at the ruler's side, and the affair repeatedly failed.
translations.idiomatic: Xun wished to assassinate the Han ruler but could not approach him; each time at birthday felicitations he would bow and advance step by step, but was blocked by those at the ruler's side, and the affair repeatedly failed.
